text: What you hope will happen if you want to say you build it and they will come, but you have the potential to grow that part of the city. >> When David I talked about and his team talked about the renewal, I said, "We can give you the money for the name, but let's keep working on how we develop the community aspects of it." >> The leadership understands the vision of where everybody wants to go, and I I think that's what excites me so much to see what's happened in that 30 years and what I think is going to happen next 30 years. title: Lamar Jackson Joins The Lounge | Baltimore Ravens
text: [music] >> Welcome into Lounge. I'm Ryan Mink here with Garrett Downing and we are thrilled to sit down with the number one player in the NFL. We don't care what the voters say. It's voter fraud, voter malpractice. We don't care [laughter] who they are. They're probably the same voters that didn't give you the MVP when you deserved it. They're the same people. >> [laughter] >> The one and only Lamar Jackson. So >> Appreciate that one. >> Lamar, you know what? Let's just get it out of the way here. What was your reaction [laughter] when you saw the top 100 list? >> Uh I was I was cool with it. I I really didn't care. You know, I play football. I don't really care about where people ranking me. >> Yeah, exactly. That's how you made it this far, man. It's don't listen to the nonsense. >> Yeah, no doubt. No doubt about it, man. >> Yeah, that's funny. You've always kind of been a guy like you've been in the spotlight for a long time since you were a young player in college. Like there's always been a spotlight on you. But I also have always marveled at your ability to just do your thing the way you want to do it and you don't really seem to care too much about the outside noise. Do you pay attention? Does any of that stuff motivate you? How do you approach approach all the noise that surrounds you? >> Uh man, if I don't I don't look for the noise, you know, pretty much it finds me. >> It finds me, you know, like earlier in my career I used to like respond to certain things I would see. I'm like, "What you talk like you know, stuff like that." But you know, I just I just grew grew more like just read my Bible, you know, getting closer to God and I'm reading the Bible and I'm seeing like that is it comes with the territory. So I I really don't care about it. >> So your your faith has been something that's kind of helps you deal with all of the attention that's on you? >> Yeah, because I'm knowing like in the word it tells us like we're not battling flesh and blood, you know, we we battling like spiritual things. You know, the principalities of this world. So I'm seeing that and I know I can't control it. So the only way I can control it is me just being me. >> Well, what I love is that every time there's something pops up, right? >> Yeah. >> Some questions or something. Every time you answer those and it feels like emphatically the the year prior or the year after. How much how much do you feel like, you know, there is this kind of chip on your shoulder at some point to to prove people wrong or whatnot because we all go back to the not bad for a running back quote, right? And I think look, we'll just plan it right now. Not bad for 69 would be [laughter] that would be kind of lit. I'm not going to lie. Is there any part of you that still is like, all right, all right, I'll show you? >> Oh, that's every year. That's every year. That's going to be every year, you know, I love the game. And if you love the game like I do, it's going to always be a chip on your shoulder. You want to win. You want to prove yourself You want to prove yourself better than you were the year before or the year prior stuff like that. So, that's all I'm doing. Just proving myself right. I really don't care about the naysayers, you know, this I told you guys this before, they're going to always be around. >> Yep. >> They're going to always be around. >> Mhm. Well, it's been a busy off season for you. You've done a lot of things. One of the things that I thought was really fun was you getting your jersey retired >> high school. So, you go back to your high school, you have the jersey retirement ceremony. Walk me through that. Like what did that mean to you cuz it seemed like it meant a lot to you. What what did that mean to you and just how cool was it to be back in that environment? >> Uh it did mean a lot to me because my one of my former teammates, uh Trequan Smith, he had uh like pretty much just got that put out there like, man, we want to retire, you know, Lamar's jersey. He reached out to me about it like talking about it. I was like, oh, that's cool, you know, I've been in the league for a long time now, you know, I done went through college. But then for him to tell me that and then it happens for him to be the head coach of the former high school that we both played at. >> Mhm. >> It was just a dope experience for me all around and then he was playing against another one of our teammates who was the head coach at uh uh >> Okay. >> I want to say Olympic Heights. I don't want to get this I believe it's Olympic Heights. And I'm like, man, this is just a a surreal experience for me. So, I just was thrilled about that situation. >> Is it Is it cool when you get a chance to go back and see the way that you are looked at by kids who are there today in the community. Like you are a beacon of light I think for a lot of people probably in your hometown and your high school. What did that mean to you? >> Man, it means a lot. I know a lot of younger younger generation of kids just looking up at me. So I know I have to do the right thing at all times, you know. That's it. That's all that matters, you know, just guys looking up to you coming from where you come from. Want to be be where you at, you know, or be who you are. It's like I don't want you to be me. I want you to be yourself. Be like Jesus if anything. Be be a good person, but I just know I got to shine my light in a different way, you know, and that's just being me. Being respectful, knowing kids looking up to me, you know, working hard, just giving back to the community as much as possible. I feel like it's small, but at the same time it's big for kids. >> Another thing we saw this off season was your boxing. You know, you're working on that right hook a little bit. >> I thought about bringing some boxing gloves in here for you. >> Yeah, exactly. Yeah. >> Tell us the the story behind that and how do you think that it's going to help you this season? >> Uh just cardio. That's what I did it for. Me and Z actually. Me and Z just cardio. We was working out. We would work out like 6:00 in the morning, 7:00 in the morning. Then we would go box, you know, for extra cardio. So that's pretty much what I was doing it for. >> That's awesome. >> Whose idea was it? Like was it your idea? Was it Z's idea? Did a trainer approach you with it? >> Nah, it was my idea. I know someone, a friend of mine, he's he was actually doing it. You know, he was actually boxing and stuff like that, but training, not not to be a boxer. He's in the tech world, but he was he just told me to come down, you know, just train. And I'm like, "Yeah, that's a good workout." So I told Z, "Man, let's go work out. You know, let's go boxing." Just been doing it ever since. >> Do you feel like you're in phenomenal shape, better shape than even previous years? >> Yeah, I actually do. I feel like I should have started earlier in the off season. It would have been better off for me. >> Yeah, yeah, that's cool. It is a great workout. It's it's it's really good. >> every almost like every part of your muscles. >> Yeah, it's good. >> Well, just going into this training camp, it seems to me like when I when I have seen you in the building, on the practice field, the vibes seem sky-high. That's the way like for you and the team, it just seems like the energy and the vibes are are really high going into this training camp. Am I reading that right? How are you looking at it? >> Uh you're reading it right. You're reading it correct. So, I'm I'm hyped, man. Uh I I believe just because we we finished the season off in a way we wasn't accustomed to, you know? So, um just that, you know, uh new new guys around, you know, just a whole new team basically, you know, and I'm a vet now. I've been a vet probably 2 years, I'd say. >> But, it's like now I'm really a vet, so it's like, man, it's just a real it's it's just a it's just overwhelming in a good way, though, in a positive way. It's fun. >> What has this coaching change been like for you? >> Oh my goodness. Uh it's great. Like, it's I'm always thinking. I'm always thinking, man, Deck can just quiz you at any time. Like, "Hey, what you got on this right here?" It's like, uh >> Just like passing in the hallway? >> No, not not necessarily, but we in the meeting room. Uh he'll walk in, you know, Coach Izzy uh Coach knows Coach Marcus in the uh room with us. And uh Izzy just come in, go to talking and be like, "Hey, so, if I What's What's this place limited to?" Stuff like that. So, it's like you got to be on your A-game at all times. And I love that, you know? It's like challenging in a good way, different terminology, um different movements with the offense. It's it's just great all around. I feel like the guys just joined in on the new system and we we loving it. We loving it. >> I I know you talked in mini camp we joked about Declan Doyle cussing you out on the practice field to challenge you and and kind of hold you accountable. I think that there's some perception that exists for today's athletes that guys don't want to be challenged by coaches. You know, it's like you don't it's you see that at different levels, I think. But, it in hearing from you at mini camp, I felt like you're like, "No, challenge me. Like, I want to be held accountable. I want you to like bring the best out of me." And it seems like that's exactly what he's doing. >> Yeah, that's exactly what he's doing. And um you know, I've been coached like that all my life though. You know, since youth football I started in youth football. High school I'll say relax but I had certain coaches that are you know, get on me if he see you know, just just holding me accountable, you know, cuz he know what type of player I am and my team and my former teammates as well. College I had Bobby Petrino. There's no discrimination. You know, you getting coached you getting coached how you supposed to get coached. Challenged all times and that's what I'm receiving from coach Decklin. You know, he's challenging us and that's pretty much what I want and I feel like every player should want that. You want the the coach to bring the best out of you. I don't feel like I know it all. You know, even if I feel like I know something now teach me I want to see your point of view of this. You know, so that's pretty much what I like and that's what coach is showing me. >> And I think it's like a fine line of like coaches being able to hold guys accountable while also being respectful and like not just cussing you out for the sake of it. And like we had we we talked to Jesse on the podcast last week and he talked about how Decklin has this great ability to to hold guys accountable in a respectful way. >> Absolutely. >> And like that that really seems seems to matter. Um do you think the age like you guys are the same age? You're both 29 years old. Like does that is that factor in at all? Is that helpful from the connection standpoint? >> Um we probably probably will watch the same I'll say prime show or something like that. Prime show or something like that but our age it doesn't mean anything cuz respect is respect. You know, his title is coach so I'm going to treat him like a coach. I don't care if he's 50, 29, 28. Um I don't care if he was younger than me. You know, he's probably a month older than me but it really don't matter. His his title is coach so I'm going to treat him like a coach and I want him to coach me like he's my coach. >> Right. Then you you won an MVP in Greg Roman's first year as offensive coordinator. You won an MVP in Todd Monken's first year as offensive coordinator ship and second also. >> There's a there's a trend here. There's a pattern here, right? What is it about first year coordinators you feel like that gets you really going? >> Ah I can't call it. I really can't call it. I probably new system, um defenses can't approach us the same way they've done in years past. Um Things have changed, you know, different different uh like I said earlier motions and stuff like that, different formations, um different guys in different areas. So, everything is just different. So, how can you contain it basically? >> Well, I think that's kind of the mark of a special player, right? It's like just when people think they have an idea of how to defend you. >> Now now, we're going to change it up and now you're going to have to deal with something new, right? Like the the best players, regardless of sport, that happens when when they can change. And I feel like you're in that same boat. Like you've adapted and changed with each coordinator. >> How do you see yourself adapting and changing now with Decklin? >> Uh smooth, but like we talked about earlier, challenging. He challenging me each and every day. Uh whether it's footwork, you know, uh whether it's just, you know, just get the ball rolling, you know, let's get to the line of scrimmage, execute at a fast tempo. And even though it's a new system, but I want you thinking. You know, in the classroom, he told me that earlier, you know, in the classroom it's easy for you to just get this right, but when you get out to the line of scrimmage, is the execution fast enough, you know, and I like that. I actually like that. >> Do you What's your role in giving him guidance of what you like? Like when he first started, when him and Jesse first started, do you sit down with them and say like, "Here's how I see the game. Here's what I would like to see the offense look like." Walk me through that process a little bit. >> Yeah, pretty much all of that. You know, they came down to Florida, Coach Jesse and Deck, talked to me. They asked me a little bit about that. It you know what? It wasn't even about that the first meeting with those two. It was about, you know, just getting a feel for me, I'm getting a feel for those guys. And um when I came up, you know, our OTAs, we meet. And it's just like, "Okay, so how do you see How do you see like, you know, how you study? Um how do you see this and that?" And and we just want to piggyback piggybacking off of each other. >> What's your favorite route to throw? >> Whatever wants a touchdown. >> Whatever wants a touchdown. I like to score. It really doesn't matter cuz you can throw a slant and it can go to the house. You can throw a bubble and go to the house. I like to put points on the board. So, whichever one put us in the end zone. >> Yeah, I like I like that. That play sounds good. [clears throat] >> I [laughter] love it. >> Did that Did it mean a lot to you when when Decklin and Jesse came down to Florida and just got to know you and spent time with you? >> Oh, absolutely. Absolutely, man. It means a lot. You know, they told me, you know, they I was a part of the reason, you know, those guys came. Wanted to take the job, you know, plus there Harry Carr and the rest of the unit and rest of my guys. But, it definitely meant a lot to me. >> That's cool. I think a lot of people, as we talked about, you know, there's always questions about different things, right? And you've proven everybody without beyond the shadow of doubt who you are as a passer, right? >> And now, but the crazy part is like people are like, "Well, can he still run like he used to run?" That >> It's full circle, man. You have to go back to the beginning. >> [gasps] >> What do What do Hey, that's so funny. >> Hey, that's [laughter] crazy. >> Right. >> It like >> What do you say I mean, obviously last year, the injuries, obviously. Like all of us in this building knew what was kind of going on, right? But, like what do you say to the people who are like, "I don't know. Lamar's average yards per whatever, you what I mean?" Like, what do you say to that? >> Man, I just play football. You know, just like you said, you know, early on in my career, "Oh, he can't throw." It was "I can't throw. He was a running back." Now, it's "Oh, he's not running enough." Like, it's pick your poison. I'm the type of player you got to pick your poison, you know, and I'm I'm approaching defenses whatever they give me. >> I'm going I'm going to take that. You know, I'm trying to score. I'm trying to move the ball down the field. So, if I don't have to run, I'm not going to run. I'm not going to force anything. You know, I'm trying to win. So, you got to use your mind. >> Yep. Yep. We asked you a lot about Decklin Doyle, but I also want to get your take on Jesse Minter and the way that you guys have connected and the way that he's running things here early in training camp and what your impressions have been of him as a head coach. >> Oh, yeah. Coach Jesse, he's cool, bro. He's like, "You got to worry about himself." He's just like, "Man, that guy, I like that guy right there, man. He's smooth. >> Just yesterday he was getting on one of the players. I never seen him get on anyone. You know, not even OTAs early on, you know. Just yesterday he got on one of the players. And then after like, you know, we break down, I'm like, "Coach, that's my first time seeing you get after someone." So he's like, "You know, sometimes, you know, you got to." >> Cool way, too. It was like, "Yeah, I understand." He's just cool, man, and I honest to me, I I feel like he gets it, you know, he he's a he's a a team like a a team player guy. Like team player coach. Like he's all about the guys, you know, "How do you feel about this? You know, how should we move with certain things, you know? Okay, this might be too much." He's like he sees it. Like he sees like we was just running the other day and then he was like, "All right, tomorrow we're not going to do that. >> We're not going to run after practice. We're just going to do this, you know." And it's like, "Okay, he gets us. He understands. It's dope." >> Do you think like the little things like the be your best competition at the end of practice >> and the way that he's kind of structured things, do you feel like that is helping I It seems to me like it's helping camaraderie. Like I watch that that session at the end of practice and it seems like everybody's having a great time and building the chemistry. But then it also seems like it's putting you guys in the mindset that at any moment you're going to have to be called upon to deliver on the big play or the big moment of a game. How do you feel like all of that stuff is going to help you once you get into the season? >> Uh yeah, like like you said, you know, just building the chemistry from from that standpoint from day one. We got a lot of young guys in now. And in this league, you know, it's any given moment, any given play, it might be the next man up. So just with guys just having the confidence in themselves, you know, I can be I can play with these guys or my teammates looking at them looking up to me looking at me to hold myself accountable or he holding me accountable. That's pretty much what's a pretty much what's coach been pretty much preaching to us all. And that's what it's been. And I feel like the sky's the limit. It's like there's no limit for us to have success with a coach like that or just talking to the team in such a manner. Yeah, smooth. >> We talk about all the the coaching turnover, but there has been some roster turnover, obviously your guys they likely unfortunately you know going and stuff, but you know you you still have some of your dogs, you know what I mean? Zay, Mark, Derek, all of bait, you know, those guys, right? And now you have this young crop of of pass catchers, two rookie wide receivers, you know, Jacoby and Elijah, then you have the two tight ends, you know, Matt and Quez and so just kind of how do you look Tez obviously a big part of that. How do you look at the arsenal of weapons around you as you go into this year? >> It's all good on paper. You know, I'm I'm I'm not a paper guy. I'm a we get on the field and we show. I'm I'm a lead by example type of guy. I really don't care about the paper aspect. Like yeah, a lot of good names, but it's what we going to do when we get on the field. How we how will we produce? You know, how will we move the ball? How we challenge it challenge ourselves? And that's pretty much how I'm rolling. Like I love all my guys. Like all the guys who we have it looks and sound good, but once we get on that field, let's just prove it. >> Do you like having these young guys all four rookies in there that are looking to you, right? And like you're establishing that connection with them and you're coaching them, I'm sure. Like is that another exciting part of this season for you is I have these young talented dudes that I get to work with, you know? >> I don't I don't consider myself old, but it's like these guys just just yesterday I believe coach I think it was coach Izzy or Deck. It was like when you was in your rookie in the league, those guys were like in 10th grade. >> So it's like for me to be talking to these guys about like how I see the game and you know, how my feel for the game is is cool. Like it's really cool to me, you know, I find it funny sometimes though cuz I feel like I was just a rookie. >> You're right. You can't say you're old cuz that makes us ancient. All right, so you are >> I don't call myself OLD. I'M ONLY 29. >> IT IS CRAZY THOUGH. I WAS THINKING ABOUT THIS THE other day because I'm like, you're one of the players in my career here. I've been here for 15 years that I've worked with the longest. Like you're up there now. It is like, wow, it's kind of crazy thinking about it in those in those terms. In in in talking about the weapons, I got to get your take on Zay because I just feel like Zay is going to have a monster season. Like he's been great, but I think that like his game could take even another leap and people are going to be talking about him after the season as one of the best receivers in the game. >> [snorts] >> Bro, it's like it's nothing to deal with him. Like he's We've seen it since his rookie year. You know, he's been the same player and he on it. All he know is grind. Like that's the thing with Zay. All he know is work. 5:00 in the morning, work. 5:00 in the morning, work. Like 7 days out the week almost. It's like, bro, when you going to break? I'm asking him. I'm like, when your off day? >> Oh, Sunday. >> Sunday? You working Monday, too? Like we in off season. Like chill a little bit. He like, Just chill a little bit, man. But man, his work ethic is extremely out of this world. That's why he's the type of player he is though. And this year I feel like he will have a monster year, man. Hopefully a record breaking year cuz the work Like I said, the work ethic that's I'm going to speak on that all the time. He's He's a smart player. But that work ethic it going to take him way farther. Like way farther. Like he's he different. He is different. >> Does he push you? Cuz I know you guys train together. Like we're talking about in the boxing. >> He pushed me to wake up at 5:00 in the morning >> on during the off season cuz it's like I wait till probably 9:00 or something to work out. He calling me. I'm like, man, I overslept. >> Not even that. Like my phone I have my phone down cuz I'm probably tired from the day before working with him. I'm like, all right, coach. Like just call me at 5:00. You know, what time we going? All right, 6:00. All right, I'm sleeping. >> He probably going to call me like seven times. Like four 4:00 or 5:00 in the morning. I'm like, bro, I did not get that call. >> I overslept, man. Like his his grind is out of this world, man. I appreciate him working that hard, bro. >> Well, speaking of some players you got, too, the offensive line, right? The big investments that the team made there, bringing in bringing back John Simpson, you know, drafting Ben Cleveland in the first round, now pick up Ethan Posic, a veteran center, you know. Obviously last year we saw kind of it goes uneven at times, right? How how do you feel with this offensive line? Because I always feel like, man, you give Lamar a little bit of time, it's game it's game over, right? How do you feel going into the year with this line? >> Pretty much the same way I feel about our skill players. You know, it's good on paper, you know, we just got to show it. We got to prove it. You know, prove how talented we are, not just Yeah, the name speak for itself. It's like, no, each and every year you got to go out there and prove your name speak for itself until you're done. So. >> Yep. I think sometimes people get things a little twisted and they're like, well, Lamar, he can always escape pressure, right? That's Lamar, right? >> How much better is Lamar Jackson when he's has that protection? >> Oh, man, they're going to see. They're going to see the world, see. Eventually, they're going to see. >> How do you I'm curious going into this year, there's all there's always expect expectations on you and the team, but when you look at whatever the odds for the Super Bowl and all that, like the Ravens are a team that are in the mix there. The people are mentioning it's like, hey, they could get to the Super Bowl. They're one of those one of the teams in the in that group. How do you handle those expectations? And and what are your expectations going into this year? >> I was feeling just how they're feeling. Like I expect to be there, too, each and every year, you know, um but we have to we have to start it's starting now, though. You know, it start each and every week. It don't just happen in February. We have to get there first, you know, the expectations is you're getting better each and every day until we're in February until we playing in February until we at that stage. Like the the uh the whatever [snorts] they're putting us oh, yeah, I expect them to be, you know, this record or you know, just guessing the record, whatever the predictions, all of all of that. But it's like, bro, we got to get better now. Each and every week, each and every day, um in the film room, um recovering, all that play a part, you know, even though at the end of the season some guys are banged up, but a lot of guys push through and and, you know, meet their team help their team go to the next uh level, win the Super Bowl, win in the playoffs. So, we got to start now and training account. Each and every day just build on that consistently, just being consistent, uh practicing hard, you know, being smart. I feel like we'll we'll we'll get to where we want to go, but until then we just got to focus on each and every day. Meetings, practice, meetings, practice until Sunday, win games, you know, and just so on until we get there. We can't focus on the Super Bowl without producing now. We were just 89, we finished 89, 98 last year. >> We we didn't make the Super Bowl. We were talking about it, but we didn't produce, so it's like, why talk about it? Got to be about it now. Finish games, finish practice, keep getting better. And the promise land will be ours. >> Is that something that you learned over time? Because I feel like earlier in your career, we all know you want to win a Super Bowl. We all know that, okay, everybody is aware of that. But it seems like maybe earlier in your career you were thinking Super Bowl and now it seems like you're thinking just today. Like is that a mindset shift? >> Yeah, cuz younger my in early on in my career uh it was like like rookie year and stuff like that. It was like, yeah, NFL is and nothing different, but it's like, oh yes, it is, cuz it ramp up sometimes. You know, certain depending on who you playing, uh depending on the atmosphere of the game, guys might come out there and have your number. And not just necessarily you, but the team. It's like, damn, we're not producing like we we're not moving the ball. Like what's going on? Why we starting slow? Why we finishing slow? Certain games I felt like in the in my career, you know, throughout years, we didn't produce how we supposed to. And that's just what me growing over time and seeing that is like we got to get better now. We got to work on things right now. We got to get better now and finish in practice. Cuz just probably 2 days ago we started off shaky, finished shaky. And like coach talked about that and I'm like, damn, we we went through that years and years in the past. We need to work on stuff like that now. So, when the season come, playoffs come, you know, and so on, we won't ever have that situation happen. You know, we Not every game going to be perfect, but we won't start slow, we won't finish slow. >> Right. Do you think that's the result in part because of 2019? Like you're just cutting through dudes. Like that team felt unstoppable, right? That like it at that point it was like, man, this this is kind of easy. You know what I mean? Do you feel like that's what kind of affected that mindset? >> young mindset. That's the young mindset. Like, oh, this it's easy. Let me go out there. We played Titans. Those guys like, we want to beat them. They 14 and two. People not expecting us to beat them. Right. We was predicted to win. Right. You know, all of that high expectation. The Ravens going to roll through them. And they come out and beat us like 28 to 12 or something, six or something. Like it's like bro, we didn't finish we didn't start fast, we didn't finish nothing. It was all downhill from the get-go. So, it's we getting training camp and like I said, you know, this whole process me and all of that, the challenges from coach Decklin and coach Jesse, we need all of that. Cuz that's going to help us in the long run. >> Does that mean Does that mean the ping pong tables are still out? >> I mean I mean it's a new team. It's a new season. >> New season, okay. >> Yeah, we get a chance. We get a chance, but we got to stay locked in though. Don't just start BSing and start just sitting around thinking it's cool. I don't care we start off five and 0, six and 0. >> We got to finish like We got to finish the whole season. And that's going to be different. And it's that adaptability and that versatility and that confidence to play whatever game is needed to be played. That's a successful offense. So, um I know that's not a number that you can go look up in week seven and see whether or not we're successful based on that answer, but I know it when I see it. If someone could guarantee you right now that you would lead the league in one category, not wins, but one [laughter] other category, what what would be your request on off >> points? [laughter] >> No, I know. I mean, >> yeah, probably. Yeah, not necessarily, but you you can doesn't mean they got to score a lot of points, you know. Um, [clears throat] you know, that's a hard like listen, there's a lot of different there's measures that are going to point towards efficiency. There's meas measures that are point towards explosiveness. There's measures that try to balance both. Um I'm not going to pinpoint one over the other. I would kind of defer my answer to what I give Ben. >> It's always been a tough wide receiver room just to get a seat in. Do you anticipate that even being at a higher >> level this summer? >> Yeah, you know, I think we've built depth at that position. Obviously, um we know that run that that room runs through uh Jamanti. Um but there'll be some really fun battles towards the back of that room and um we'll see guys are going to have opportunity to show what they can do, not only offensively, but show how they can contribute to this team on special teams. That's a big part of when you're talking about a fifth, a fourth, a fifth, a I mean really everybody past the third guy, and even the third guy is going to have to do something. Um so how those guys are able to perform for Darren. Um and then given the fact that we have Jamar and T uh you know those opportunities to execute when they come up because they might not there might not be a ton of them and it's pass game opportunity and it's also what can you do to contribute in the run game on normal downs uh because of how we play. um that'll go a long way to determining the opportunity and the reps and um I'm excited to see who steps up in that way. A >> lot of conversation about team chemistry >> and how important that's been. Why has it been this offseason maybe different than it's been in years past and what you've seen from these groups? >> Well, I I think that's a little bit of an ongoing story, right, as to how that develops. You you can develop in some of that in OTAAS, right? But I think the the crux of that gets developed in camp where we're together, you know, for a lot the days here a lot longer. It's back to backtoback days. it's not uh um and we're involved here in beatings longer and so I think a lot of that is still yet to be determined but I do have a great feel um I have a good feeling I guess about the guys we've brought in and the you know I think it's the level not only experience but the success they've had as as both as players individually but then some collectively bringing in you know multiple Super Bowl champions here we're bringing in all pro players and so I I think with that comes a level of respect um not that we didn't have some of those types of players here before, but I think when it's new and you're bringing it from different backgrounds and you try to combine that, right? I mean, that brings a a renewed sense and that's that's what's great about the game that we play, right? It's it's so many different backgrounds from so many different people all get one, you know, together to try to mesh that and that's what makes it exciting to me. >> Joe said that this is the most talented roster on paper that he's played with here in Cincinnati. You are the longest tenure assistant in the league. Is this the most talented roster that you've been? >> Oh man, you're really challenging my memory. Um, we we we've had some talented rosters way back, too. But I probably tend to agree with them. I I think this is, you know, we've helped maybe fill in some holes, fill in some blanks that I don't blanks, but uh we we've upped the level of of uh respectability, I think, at some of those positions. So, I would probably tend to agree with that. Um, but you're you're dating me when you start to ask me about some of those teams we had back early on. There were some pretty talented teams we had back early on, too. you know, 05, 06, those are some pretty good teams back then, too. But I I probably tend to agree this this is this on paper it feels that way. Well, of course, we'll see what happens. Somebody punches in the mouth. That's when I really feel those guys come along. >> Along those lines, Darren, what is the characteristic you value most when you're, you know, you've seen so many Bengal teams here that you value the most that leads itself over the course of a season to success? >> You're talking just team in general, >> team. >> Um, toughness. I I I I think that that's part of it. There's a lot of them I think that have equal weight, right? Intelligence is one. Um toughness certainly is one. Um you know, you have to have such great team players. You know, I I I think gone are the days of when there's so many individ where you know, one player can take over a game like like like they can like it used to be able to. So, you know, uh I I think having great team players who are intelligent and who are tough and who love to be who love the game and love the process that that comes to take to prepare for a game I think are all big factors for me are ones that I would look for. >> What about what have you appreciated the most about Zack Taylor and what you've learned about him his entire tenure here? Well, I I think his ability to um let guys do their job, and not that it hadn't that hadn't been the case before, but I have a lot of respect for Zack, I think, knows what what uh he majors in. And uh he knows that he's a great offensive mind. So, you know, I I think that, you know, as as the head coach, it's his responsibility for all three phases, don't get me wrong, but you know, I I think that he helps uh support me as a special teams coordinator. um with personnel. Um I think he has a solid feel for how the the game day roster is put together, the 48 guys we're we're looking for. And I think he trusts me um to handle my area and trust me to handle what I do. So, that's one thing I really respect is is he uh um I I think he'll be hands-on if he needs to be, if he feels like he needs to be, but I I do feel like that he trusts me um to do my job and be, you know, a productive part of our productive third of the team. So, that's a huge area respect to have. >> There's not going to be a lot of pressure on Zack this year and all to perform. It seems like he actually handles that pretty well. Why Why does Zach handle pressure maybe better than other coaches? >> Um I guess it's because of his very calm demeanor, right? I I don't I don't I don't ever I mean maybe you would know more than I would about ever seeing him get ramped up other than somebody other than officials, right? You know, he's good at that. Uh I've seen that happen multiple times, but I I I I think, you know, his demeanor and his ability to stay on an even keel is very good. He has a very good he does a very good job of relationships with with players. And I I I think that uh he works with guys well. And I also think that when it when it comes time for him to make a stand, he'll make a stand. Uh but but I I do think that his ability to, you know, reach reach each player, each guy from different backgrounds, it's it's tough for him because he's the head coach of the offense, right? He's the head coach of our team, yet he's the head coach for offense, but he still has to have relationships with players on defense, but the majority of his time has to be spent with the offense. Um, so I think his ability to, you know, get to those players on defense or get to the guys on special teams that matter, I think is a really really good quality he has. >> When you look at returner, Charlie's proven things. Keshan really popped at the end of last year. How do you view that spot this summer? >> Well, I I view it as a pretty good competition, right? I mean, Charlie's the income of guy. I mean, he naturally should be. He's proven he can do it. scored three times in three years, but you know, he's got to be able to stay on the field. And so, you know, I think having uh somebody like Keshan here pushing him in that regard is a huge factor. And and I see it as as a good competition. I see it as a competition as we go through training camp that they'll get a lot of I mean, both those guys are going to get a ton of reps >> and I think it's just part of the equation, right? I think also the other part of the equation is what they do on offense. Like who do they feel most comfortable with on offense and if there's a deciding factor, it'll be what they do in in the uh as a return. Just having snapper holder kicker first time in a handful of years kind of ironed out. >> Yep. >> Is that a major advantage? >> Major. Yeah, major advantage. You know, I since this is the I mean, we were so fortunate here for so long to have, you know, the same snapper and Clark and the same punter and Kevin and those are just main stays, right? A few of the kickers change, but I knew there's going to come a time where this is all going to change. And we tried to put it together in pieces, you know, a little at a time. It all kind of end up happening at once. And you know, we I feel like we've finally settled on the three guys um who we're going to have going to have here for a long period of time. So, I believe it's a major advantage for us to go into year three. I believe that those three guys can be will be a weapon for us that we use whether it's flipping to field with Ryan, um whether it's hopefully controlling the ball better in the plus 50 with Ryan, plus 50 punting and then the ability for Evan to hit long kicks and be consistent on kickoff. So, it's a big advantage for

title: Zac Taylor on the Bengals' Talent, Confidence & Chip on Their Shoulder Entering Training Camp
text: Anybody you guys don't expect to start practicing out the jump on Wednesday? Besides B.J.? >> B.J. and uh Josh Gattis. >> Okay. Anybody else you think will be limited that you guys >> Uh Connor Lu or we're going to monitor Connor Lu. He's coming off the injury. Um he's done a great job handling everything he can handle. Now we we just have to do a great job managing him over the course of training camp. >> Is he Is he cleared for everything? >> Yeah, he's cleared for everything. Yep. Yep. >> I want to follow up on that specifically with Josh Gattis. Are you able to say what what's the reason why he's out? Chance? >> N- Nothing major. >> Nothing major? >> Yeah. It'll be I I don't want to put a time stamp on how long it'll be, but um been really impressed with him in his time here. I know he's fought two injuries now he's had to go through, but um that doesn't change my opinion on the things that he's done to to put himself in a good position to compete for first spots on our team. >> I want to follow up on something Al just spoke about and that is your challenge to the coaching staff to make sure that the best players were on the field being utilized in their best way. I'm paraphrasing probably poorly, but uh paraphrasing that. What does If you could expand upon that, Zac, what that means? >> I think uh we got a lot of good players in all three phases. And so I think just by the time you get to the first game of the season, there's a lot of things we got to work on as a team that sometimes you just got to put in the training camp so you got it in your back pocket. But as we come out of this thing, we got a lot of great players that that other teams will fear. And I want them to have the utmost confidence in the work they put in, the the confidence in the position we're putting them in to do what they do best, and to to cause problems on the other team. And so I think we got a lot of those players that are that tier. We got a lot of players that have a really critical role to play for us that are to an extent glue guys, really really good players um who are going to be play off some of these these high-tier players we got. So I'm really excited about the collection of talent that we've got on our team and the role everybody's going to play in order for us to be successful. >> Does that necessarily meaning mean having them on the field as much as possible, or is there a balance there to rest and >> Well, I think that's that's uh per game conversation, you know, based on the position they play and and the role they got to play there, but um when we're out there, we always want to put our guys in a position where they got a ton of confidence they're being used the right way to go go make some plays. >> How how'd you evaluate Chase Brown in kind of the off-season he's had what do you expect out of him this year? >> Well, the same for Chase. Chase has always been a guy that you can trust to put in the work to try to make himself a better player. I think he played at a really high level last year. Had a lot of production for us in the run and the pass and in protection. I mean, he was there's some clips of him being absolutely tremendous in pass protection last year. And so again, he's got a lot of weapons that can be dispersed a lot of different ways. Um I'm excited to see what he can bring to the table for us. >> I know it's not offense, but defensively nickel corner, how excited or interested are you to see how that's going to play out? It feels like there's five or six different guys that can >> Yeah, I think there's a lot of opportunity there. Jaylen obviously is a guy we've we've gained a lot of trust in over the last seven years, six years. And hearing that opportunity particularly at the last part of the last season. Came into the spring, he's a great communicator, he understands the defense. and there's other guys you get a chance to look all across the secondary to see what roles these guys can play even if they're not the starter, how can we get them on the field? How can they play a different role for us in a different defensive package? And so I think there's a lot of opportunity there not just at nickel corner, but across the board at defense back opportunities guys can create for themselves. >> How about what do you have to be good you guys have moved Dax around a lot. >> Yeah. >> He seems comfortable outside. Is that something that you you want to keep him? >> Yeah, correct. And and people can easily misconstrue when you're in a known passing situation and and a corner goes inside, that doesn't mean he's playing nickel, you know, so but in the normal down situations, Dax absolutely absolutely has grown as an outside corner. That's where we want him to play. That's absolutely where he's going to play. But But then there's going to be times with any corner that they go inside for coverage reasons. Um, but again, Dax has done a really good job growing out there and and that's where we want to leave him. >> What do you like about Al Golden after working with him for three years in the box? >> Well, I'm not having just worked with him for a year. I've worked with him for three years. >> role, yeah. >> I think just the way he communicates with the staff and the players. Um, the work he puts in to make sure we're doing the right things and we're doing it at a high level. And no detail goes unnoticed. No fundamental goes uncoached. I think it's As far as that goes, he's one of the most detailed coaches I've ever been around in my lifetime in terms of um, his time on task and what he's asking the coaches and the players to do. And that's going to really take shape over the course of the season. Really slowed down for a lot of guys last year after the bye. You saw a lot of young players get better. And I think that's going to really pay off for us this season, uh, especially with a lot of the veterans that we've added to the mix. >> How do you capture >> I'll go ahead. >> Go on. >> How do you capture all the excitement around the added pieces and the development of the players that you have had going into this camp this season? >> I think now the the excitement part is for the fans and the media. And now it's on us to get to work and make sure we're solving all the problems and not making re- repeat mistakes and really playing fast and with a lot of confidence. And so that that's our task. Um, there's not much for anybody watching us to do until the first game hits against Tampa Bay. So I expect there to be excitement, but but for us it's just let's put our heads down and get to work. >> Any major changes in camp and how you guys structure things this year? >> Not major changes. No, little things that I'll focus on internally with the guys, but but nothing structurally, um, that's a significant change from last year. >> You guys have done the two on one off pretty I think it was all last year, maybe the year before that, but you're starting with four straight days this year. Is there a reason for that? >> Um, and not really. Uh, the third day that'll be closed to the fans won't be won't be full speed action like that. It'll be a way to kind of recover a little bit uh, to avoid that structure. So, we've done a lot a lot of work. We've lost a lot of guys on the third day. A lot of guys over the last couple years, and that's every team. That's that's And so, um sometimes you can do everything you could possibly do on the third day to eliminate it, you're still going to have some issues. And so, I'm I'm trying to make one more change there to to make sure we can avoid that. >> I asked Duke about the depth along the offensive line. Last year, obviously, you guys were pretty fortunate. He was adamant that the depth is there on the offensive line, and maybe more so than even we in the media have a feel for. How about you? How What's your comfort level with the depth along the offensive line? >> There There's a lot of guys I'm really excited to watch compete. And some of them haven't gotten a lot of opportunity to showcase. Maybe we saw in the draft process. Um, we saw in training camp with other teams. But now they're here, and we get a real chance to evaluate these guys and see who can earn what roles for us. And so, I I do have a lot of confidence that it'll take shape to where we're going to have 10 guys that can really walk on the field and help us. Um, which is hard to do in the NFL. There's not 10 guys walking around on all 32 rosters that uh have always earned the opportunity to to walk out there and play offensive line in this league. And so, I think that our scouting department has done a really good job of getting guys that maybe it didn't go perfectly for them somewhere else. Or we've added them in the draft, and now we're going to give them an opportunity to earn that position. >> On this paper, is this the toughest wide receiver room to get a seat in this year? I know it's always >> almost an impossibility on the back end, but just your thoughts on how that looks >> I >> on the back end this year. >> Yeah, it's um again, it's always a question of how many we're keeping there. And that's not just competing with receivers, that's competing with other positions sometimes. I think everyone carving out a role um carving out a role that we feel like it can help us, carving out a role that we feel like it can help us in the future. Um, it's a tough room cuz we got a lot of returning players there. And then we've added guys at the end of last season. We've added guys this off season. We've added guys in the draft that'll come in here and compete. And we're open to seeing how guys do it. >> Is Cash Harris how well a true edge in your mind or is he a piece that you can kind of move around the chessboard? >> I think we got a lot of ends that you can move around a little bit, you know, and so he's a defensive end. Now now what that means evolves from package to defense package. And so I think we've got guys like him and Boye, Miles, and Shemar um said that that can all do some different things for us. Um number one, they can all rush the passer. Number two, they can all be a force in the run game. And then number three, how else can you utilize them in different schemes, different packages that help the entirety of our defense? And so I think that we've got a really good collection of guys that I'm excited to watch compete. And there's others in there. I mean, there's Isaiah Foskey. We've got a good mix of guys that I'm excited to watch go play football this training camp. >> During OTAs, Joe said that he was kind of speaking up a little more aggressively. He said he was a little more meaner in his leadership style. Have you seen a change in how he leads? >> No, I mean, I think it's always an evolution for every player in terms of how they And the biggest thing as a leader is is, you know, I just have to talk to everybody universally the same way. You know, it's it's what makes each guy get to their highest level. Same goes for me. I'm not going to talk to everybody the same way I'm talking to somebody else. And so um it's just finding I think that's that's true leadership is trying to find the best way to make everybody get to their highest level. >> That being said, what are the conversations like with Burrow as you all getting ready for training camp? Leave him alone during these times. >> Yeah, I leave him alone. Yeah, I'm not Yeah, we're going to talk plenty over the next 6 months, so. >> He said 48 touchdowns doable. Didn't hesitate. >> [laughter] >> Gave us something to write about. I think it's been done five >> he say this? >> It was like his last statement of >> Oh, in June? That would pass all for the all-time franchise record. Passing touchdowns, so. >> In a career? >> It's a big number. >> That's great. Uh yeah, I'm all for it. >> a lot on the one-yard line. >> Yeah, I'm all for it. That's sounds like a lot of checked plays on the one-yard line, that's what it sounds like. Um removing some of the the throw tags on some of the run plays, but we'll be at our best when he's at our best. So, I want I like that confidence from him. I want our best players to have an edge to them and an expectation that the rest of the team can follow suit. So, um I'm not going to stymie that in any way, shape, or form. And so, I like that he's got that confidence. >> I mean, he's always pretty wired going into any season, but given kind of the lack of success, do you feel an extra edge from him maybe this year going into this year? >> Well, I think that's everybody. I mean, to me I know when I look at standings or look at our schedule or something, we we were 6 and 11, third in the division. That's what stands out to me. You picture that division ranking, third in the division, and and every year's a new year. We got new players, all that kind of stuff, but that's what sticks with me. Um not that you need motivation, but does piss you off to an extent, you know, that that's what we did, and that's how people should see us until we prove them otherwise. And so, I can't speak for Joe and how he feels, but that's certainly how I feel, you know, coming into the season with a lot of um just a chance to to clean the slate a little bit and go do the things that we expect to do. >> Is this the most pissed off you've been going into a year? >> Uh I mean, I it's hard to compare from year to year.

title: Duke Tobin on Joe Burrow, the Bengals' Roster & Training Camp
text: All right, who's first? >> How's BJ Hill doing? >> BJ Hill's doing good. He's getting close. U, we're just going to work with him a little on the side, make sure he's ready to go. We know what BJ's all about, so we want to be uh cautious and make sure he's up to it before we put him out against other players. >> Is it ankle related that he kind of fought through last year or? >> Yeah, he had an offseason surgery and he's still working his way back from that, but he's he's very close. What is the level of anticipation for you going into this training camp? >> Um, anticipation in what regards? >> Expectation. >> Our expectation is to win every game we line up and play. That's our expectation. Period. It's about coming together as a team, maximizing every player we have uh with what we do with them and winning the game. That's our expectation. Job one is coming together as a team and and making sure everyone is on the same page and executing at their highest level they can execute within the scheme that we're putting in front of them. So that's the work that's going in right now, but our expectations are incredibly high. Joe to follow that up to Joe Maro said several times in the off season that the front office has given them given the players and the coaches everything they need [snorts] from your perspective when a player acknowledges that. What does that mean to you? >> Um well that's a good thing cuz that's the job that we're trying to do uh every year that we try to do it. We're we're trying to give the football team what it needs to go out and win a championship. that that is the only focus that we have and uh to hear players buy into that. I think that's motivating. I I think it's exciting. You know, we've got a big opportunity in front of us and we're all excited about that opportunity and uh Joe's been around good teams, you know, here and in college and in high school and everywhere else. He knows what a good team can be, but we got to go out and become a good team. We uh we have a lot of pieces that we're proud of that we have seen perform at high levels and if they can perform as a as a group at a high level then we'll really really have some. >> Are you still looking at the free agent market names like Bobby Wagner DVO Samuel kind of >> Yeah, I I'm not going to talk about any players that aren't here. But do we look at the free agent market? We look at it every day. Every single day. We're always looking at what opportunities we have. We had a lot of really good opportunities uh come to us this year and and to what this personnel department what the ownership did is respond and make those opportunities realities. So we we're always looking at opportunities. Is there something coming around the plate tomorrow? No. But there might be. Who knows? Um we're always going to judge what we can do to be better within the restrictions we have. You know, there there are restrictions in this league. There are financial and cap restrictions that are in this league that we have to work through, not only this year, but next year and the year after that. And so, all of that is a part of the puzzle, but are we looking to improve the team? We're always looking to improve the team. >> Talking about the cap restrictions, why was it important for you guys to restructure Joe's contract? Well, you got to get through the season and you have to have enough room to get through the season and we want to have a practice squad and we're anticipating at least a few injuries that we've got to uh that we've got to account for. Uh we uh we want to elevate guys when we feel the need to elevate guys. We have incentives and contracts that we have to account for. So, there's a lot of things that go into you can't zero it out going into camp. And I I think that's some people don't understand that, but you the season and do what you want to do throughout the season to keep your team at a high level. And so part of that was that uh that uh that that we needed some room. We uh we achieved what we wanted to achieve in bringing in talent and uh we'll see uh how that talent performs. >> Do you feel like this is the best roster that y'all put together going into a season since you've been here? >> Uh it's hard to see. Um, you know, we've had a lot of rosters over the years I've been here. Um, I I feel really good about this roster. I think we've got a lot of pieces that have been proven uh productive NFL players either here or elsewhere. Uh, that you can envision playing well. Uh, the group has to come together. You can have 11 separate pieces that don't play as a group and nobody looks like they're good. and you can have 11 average pieces playing as a group and suddenly you're wondering if they're a lot better than you thought they were. So, we've got to come together as a group. Um, it's a hard question to answer right now. But, uh, from what I've seen so far, uh, this is a motivated group hungry to uh, show what they can do, all 90 of them. >> Where do any potential talks with DJ Turner or Dax Hill for that matter? >> Yeah, I'm not going to talk about any potential contracts or anything like that. All of our players are under contract, which is a good feeling. That's uh that's a positive going into camp. What happens uh in the future with other potential contracts? That won't be something I'm really discussing. Do I want our players that are progressing to be here? Yes, I always want our players that are progressing to be there. I'm proud of those guys. We drafted them, they developed, and they are uh still blossoming in their career. And I think all of them sense a big opportunity not only for the football team which is number one, but they sense a big opportunity for themselves and that's that's great. I expect that all of our players to come in motivated to maximize this season both for themselves and the football team. With that in mind, Duke, a lot of people on the outside have noted how there hasn't been a lot of drama. Uh, with regard to contracts, hold outs, holdins in the organization this year. From your perspective, would you agree with that assessment that it's been a little more calm this off season? >> Um, yeah, the drama doesn't always reach us. Uh, there's a lot of drama that happens that maybe we're not as uh locked into. Um, but we feel good about where we are. are we don't have situations that are pulling us away from the main focus. And uh and that's a good position for us to be in because we can focus on continuing to improve rather than focus on issues that aren't improving us at the moment. And so, uh, yeah, it's it's the NFL and it happens in 32 different clubs and sometimes there are things that come up that are tough dealings and you have to work your way through that and uh, and if we don't have those tough dealings, it's better not to have them. >> Do you expect DJ to practice on Wednesday? >> Oh, yeah. I think all of our guys are motivated and ready to to come together as a group. So, absolutely. I don't think there's anybody that's looking to detract from that. >> When you talk about the when you assess a roster, a lot of people just focus on what they bring on the field, but how important is integrating guys like Dexter, like Jonathan Allen, like Brian Cook as far as just personalities in the [snorts] locker room and leadership and how what have you seen so far from that integration? >> Yeah, the offseason program was great. Um, we have a lot of guys who respect the new guys that came in based on what they've done at their other teams and I think a lot of those new guys have started to really earn the respect uh as individuals in our locker room and and so I've been really impressed with how the group has come together. We have a group that uh enjoys being around each other. They enjoy preparing for football. They enjoy practicing against each other. uh they they hang out outside of the building and so that those are all positives in team building, but all of the new guys that have come in have fit in great and provided us what we thought they would provide us >> given where the quarterback market sits as lewide as a whole and that could get reset here any day now as well. What's kind of the biggest challenges when looking at how to invest in that position with >> talking about potential contracts, it we want to keep our guys and what happens around the league does affect us and we'll have to we'll have to look at that and see uh how it affects us and what we can do going forward. But the specifics of of any specific position and I know what you're after and we're just not going to talk about any contract that might come. All of our guys are signed. All of our guys are motivated and we're happy about that. >> Going back to the contract question real quick on uh burrow the restructuring. Y'all have been hesitant in the past to push numbers down in the future years. Why were y'all comfortable doing that this year? You didn't do the max either. >> Well, you do it when you have need. Um and uh and we had opportunity uh that we took advantage of uh that uh that came upon us which is which was very good opportunity that came came to us and then you have to adjust after that opportunity comes to you and that's what we've done. Uh there are there are a lot of things that go into what you need throughout the course of a season and uh and we do the best analysis of that as we can and um that always exists that you can do a restructure with somebody to to do that. It does push money down to future years and we have future years that are also uh uh heavy with contracts with guys on this current team and we hope that uh this current team achieves its goals and will attack next year when the next year comes. >> Will there be restrictions for Eric all right off the bat at camp? How do you >> Not really. He's been cleared. Um, you know, there'll be a progression plan back into football that might extend beyond some of the other progression plans we have. There's there's 5day, you know, acclamation periods and so forth. We'll take it day by day and see how he's doing. He looks great right now and he looks great running around out there right now. So, he's been cleared for full activity and uh we'll see how quick that progression plan puts him back in the heavy action. Have you appreciated how sorry uh how TJ Sllayton's handled his offseason work and just seems like he's been so locked in, you know, knowing that his role may may change a bit this year. How do you view how he's >> I I think everyone is is looking at their role and trying to grow it and trying to be a major part of this team. It's a good team to be a major part of and everyone wants that role and so everyone's locked in and and TJ's locked in and I have belief in TJ that he can play a big role for us and uh and if he's locked in on that like you say I that's what I've seen and if if you're seeing it too that's good news and we want our guys trying to expand their roles trying to grow their roles and trying to be major factors for our team and he's a guy with the ability to do that >> Connor Lou, how how's his status do going into camp? >> Good. Conor's been cleared. Again, he'll have a progression plan back into the heavy action, but uh we'll see how it goes in the early parts of camp. And uh what that progression plan is, we'll uh we'll determine at a later date. >> How comfortable are you or what measures are you willing or considering to take to bolster the depth on the offensive line? >> I feel good about the depth of of our off line. We've got a lot of young guys that are that are about to take a real jump and um you can only keep nine of them on your roster. Uh that's already a problem in my mind. Maybe you keep 10 and go light somewhere else. But we've got guys that I believe in that uh given a bigger role can can come on. And um so I probably don't agree with your question, I guess. >> What about Nickel? How do you feel about Nickel, dude? [clears throat] Well, we'll see how it goes. You know, we've got guys that are competing in there, and we brought guys in this off season that'll get some competition in there. We've got uh young guys who will grow in their second and third years at that position. We've got JD, who came in, stepped in, played a big role. I don't write him off because he knows how to play football. He's comfortable, and he's really motivated, and he's talented when he's out there. So, we've got a lot of guys, you know, fighting for that spot. You can't have known quantities of all pros at 22 spots. Somebody's got to develop into those and we've got guys that I think can and uh you know the job JD did for us when he came in last year was exceptional and I look forward to seeing him progress off of that. >> Does that battle excite you? Because it seems like a lot of times if you have two people compete for a spot, someone could win it by default. But when you got four, five, six guys that could win that spot, someone's going to actually win it. You know, the job of the coaches will be to put guys in positions that they play the best. And if if if we get into camp and they feel like the guy's better outside, then he'll probably play more outside. And if we get into camp and a guy shows ability to play inside in the nickel and the slot, and suddenly we think, oh, this guy can really affect us in there, we'll move another guy in there. You know, that's the the role of the coaches is to figure out who's excelling at every spot. And um and I know we'll do that. and I'm excited about the DB group. >> There were a lot of questions on Burrow uh that came here about whether he could win longterm here. How do you feel like that progression's been and do you feel like what are you expecting out of Burrow going into this year as he enters your >> um I don't know the first parts of that, but I what do I expect out of Joe Burrow? I expect him to lead the football team and to be Joe Burrow because I've seen him do that and I know what kind of player he is. I know what kind of person he is. I know how motivated he is. So, my expectations uh are incredibly high. They're probably not as high as Joe's expectations of himself. And uh that's what's comforting. I know Joe is going to maximize himself. He's going to lead the football team in the right way. And he's going to give us a real opportunity to be a winning team this year.

Um you know, just working 3 days a week, I mean, three times a day, sorry. And just making sure that I'm ready. So, I'm pretty prepared for it. >> Again, you got to kind of unique experience than most guys coming in here. But, what's the feeling still when you're getting in a huddle with a guy like Patrick Mahomes? >> It's great, you know. Still making sure I know my assignment. Um you know, he's been he's been a great guy, too. You know, very open, you know, for me to walk to him and you know, ask questions and stuff of that nature. Um but, really just making sure I'm prepared. You know, making sure that I'm executing, knowing what I'm supposed to do, knowing my assignment. So, that when my time is ready and when I'm you know, when my time is when I'm out there, you know, he's ready to throw me the ball and he can trust me. >> One more couple more? Good? Thanks again. >> Yeah, thank you. >> Appreciate it. >> What brought you here? What kind of what brought you to Kansas City? I was I was a four-phaser through my four years in college, so I just want to keep doing that, and whatever chance I can do to get on the field, and eventually eventually develop some defensive reps, this is what I want to do. >> What do you feel like is the the base of your game? It looks like you when you when we see out there in the field, even without pads, it looks like you're a pretty physical guy, and that's on your film, too. Is that your your biggest trait, or what what else is it that you feel like you do best? >> I'd say yeah, my physicality, obviously can stand out on some tape a little bit, but I'm a pretty smart guy, able to communicate very well, and help everyone get on the same page, and clean up any mistakes from the back end to eliminate big plays. >> What goals are you setting for yourself this season and beyond? What's the veteran to draft? >> I'm trying to just take advantage of any reps I can get, you know, young guy, undrafted guy, just trying to go out there when I get my number called, go make some plays, and just capitalize on those opportunities. That's all I can ask for. >> Anybody else? Thank you. >> Thank you. >> Go ahead, guys. >> You you got a got a little bit of experience here with this team at the end of last season and everything. What's been the experience like in Kansas City for you? >> Oh, it's been great. You know, my dad stayed My dad lives in Kansas City, Missouri, you know, my brothers, my aunts, my cousins, everybody from here, you know, uh so just coming back to here, it it's been amazing. You know, Coach Reid, the the teammates, you know, the receiver room, Coach O'Shea, it it's just been great all around. >> What's one thing that stood out during mini camp? I mean, have you have you kind of felt that as I mean, as far as with since he's come in, is is there been a kind of an affinity with with Coach O'Shea? >> Oh, definitely. You know, I love Coach O'Shea. Like, he's going to be hard on me, and that's the type that's the type of coach I love I love to play for, you know, a coach that's really going to get on you, really going to tell you what you need to do, the small details, and that's exactly what O'Shea does. So, when I when I get that coaching from him, like, I I love it. Like, that's that's that's that's the type of way I want to be coached. >> What's your favorite shoes to wear in the BB? Like, it was just coming in to work, and know like nothing's given to nobody. Like, so, I know I I was going to have to come in here and do the best that I can, be the best type of player I can on and off the field, in the training room, in inside of the locker room, a great teammate. So, it's it's kind of great. >> Hey, Andrew, can you Can you just take us through the last year and a half or so for you? You started undrafted and then went to a couple teams. What is your goal for this year? >> Just uh whatever I can do to help the team. Like whatever it wherever it is.
