title: One-on-one with Shane Steichen on training camp & is he good or bad at Madden? | The Colts Show
text: You know, you got the four buttons on the Xbox. So, I'll learn those and then [music] I'll call a play, but I will know when I see the coverage on certain routes and where to throw it. And so, I might call the same play five times in a row. >> [music] >> Training camp is here. Colts players are reporting to Grand Park on Tuesday, the day this episode's coming out. This is another episode of the Colts Show, and I'm JJ Stankevitz joined by head coach Shane Steichen. We're talking camp, Shane. Summer is over. >> Let's go, baby. >> I I imagine this is like Christmas morning for you of like you get to get back into season mode. You get to go. Like what what is your level of excitement today as we report here? >> Very excited, you know, you you have the little break, you know, it's about four-week break, you know, a month or whatever it is and you're about two weeks into break and then you start getting the itch again like, all right, come on, when's training camp coming and before you blink it's here, but just preparing throughout the summer too, getting ready for training camp as well. Obviously, you do a lot of prep in the spring. Um, but then, you know, ramp it up in the summer and getting ready to go when these players come in cuz it's exciting. >> What do you do in the off-season? Like to try to take your mind off of football or I mean, can you even take your mind off of football? >> Um, it's hard. It's hard. It's always on. Um, but a lot of family time really is what I like to do with the family, you know, we like to go out west um, with the family, enjoy some time there, uh, you know, go to the beach, you know, my son's in, you know, Little League baseball. So, you know, we're doing that in the summer too as well here in Indiana and then we get a little time away and then come back and that's when you know, you're two weeks out and you start getting back in the rhythm of things and start getting ready to go, but a lot of family time in the summer. >> It's great. Glad that you're uh, you're able to get that, but yeah, here we are now. Um, let's get into let's get into camp. Look, starting with Daniel Jones, uh, what is the plan for him and I guess just what do you want to get out of these practices leading up to the season with him specifically? >> Yeah, I think with the plan with him is he's going to be ready to go day one um, and he's going to get the team reps and get the first team reps and go from there. You know, he put in so much work this off-season to get to where he's at. Um and he's been tirelessly working. He's been doing it all through the summer to be ready to go. I know he's excited. I've had some good conversations with him over the summer. Um and he's ready to go. And you know, during camp, obviously, this is a time for us to connect and compete, you know, build your identity through training camp, um and go from there, you know, and create an edge and really just so you know, similar to last year, you know, you want to start the season fast. And uh you want to come out of this thing in great shape, physical shape, you know, build the mental and physical toughness is a part of training camp and building that identity. Um and you got to do it with your actions on the field, how you meet, how you practice is a big part of it. You can't just talk about it. You got to go do it. >> With with Daniel, how different is it in terms of building that identity with him coming in as the guy this year? >> Yeah, I think it's awesome to have him back. Obviously, our starter last year and knowing, you know, he's our starter again coming into this year is huge for our football team. Um you know, just a tremendous worker um that understands it, that gets it. Um so, we're excited looking forward to year two working with him. >> Can you just kind of explain the like almost like the mind meld that you two have? Of just like the the ability to see the game through the same set of eyes. And what that does to benefit you as a play caller and then him as a quarterback? >> Yeah, I think there's a lot that goes into that, you know, the communication piece is huge. You got to be a lead communicators, you know, at the quarterback position uh and with the coach and how you talk about the game and how you want it to look and how you prepare uh certain situations that we're going to be in, certain plays, you know, how I see calling the game, how he sees it, and having those conversations throughout the week are are monumental, you know, to be successful on the field on Sunday. So, I'm looking forward to building that again this year going into year two. Obviously, it's a year two in the system. Um so, that part's awesome. So, we're not starting for, you know, from the ground. Um you know, we've built, you know, had some credibility building it together. Um and so, we're excited for that part of it. >> With Josh Downs, like how much mental space has it taken up for you of trying to get him a little more involved in this offense this year? >> Look, Josh Downs is a tremendous football player. And uh I'm excited for him going into this season. Um obviously uh going into year three four it is now for him. Um you know, getting him involved any way we can, whether it's in 12 personnel, you know, obviously he plays a lot in the slot in 11 personnel, but just trying to find different ways to get him the ball and you go through that process. You know, we'll go through that in training camp, we'll go through that during game week preps. Um but we're excited for him this year. >> I want to ask you something about tight ends and Tyler Warren, but this is more of a kind of like a general question about tight ends. Over the last five years or so, we've seen tight ends come in and be immediate impact guys as rookies in a way that like I don't remember it really being the case outside of, you know, like Rob Gronkowski. You know, even in the 2010s. Why is why why have guys like Tyler Warren been able to come in and have success? I mean, it's not just Tyler, it's Sam LaPorta, it's Cole Kmet, Loveland, Brock Bowers, these guys. >> I think part of it is they're really talented players first and foremost, but they also do create mismatches and you know, in the pass game. You know, you can get a match up against linebackers and tight ends and find different ways to get them touches, whether it's in the flat or over the middle of the field, whatever it may be. Um you know, when he can run routes and separates the way he does and finish the way he does, any way you can get the ball in his hands, it's usually pretty successful. So, we're going to continue to find ways to get him the ball just like we did last year and you know, keep growing that. >> I mean, what what do you expect to see out of Tyler during training camp now that he this is his second one. He's had a full off season to go through this program. What do you expect to see out of him? >> I think just obviously year two, you know, developing his body, just the separation that he's going to create on the top of routes. I think just the route detail and how he goes about it. I think that improves as you go on year in and year out and so I'm really looking forward to that seeing that in training >> What about the right side of the offensive line? That seems to be a pretty good area of competition for this football team. >> Yeah, for sure. We got Gonsalves and Farmer there at the right guard spot and those guys will compete and we're looking forward to that. Um and Jaylen Travis is a guy that's, you know, stepped up last year for us. Very excited about his, you know, progress that he's made from last year, you know, into OTAs and now going into training camp. So, really excited about that right side of line. >> There's something to the continuity that you have as a coaching staff on offense, isn't there? Like you've had, you know, Jim Bob as the OC, you've had, uh, you know, Cam Turner as your quarterbacks coach, Reggie Wayne at wide receiver, Tom Manning, uh, down to Tony Sparano Jr., you know, the the only real addition's been like Alex Tanney kind of on the the the higher end of the coaching staff. Just What does that do for you guys as a staff to have that continuity going into year four now? >> I think the community communication piece is huge. You know, you got to be elite communicators at the coaching position and to have a continuity on the staff, being work together, going into year four together, our staff, you know, it's pretty impressive. It's rare in this league that you get that. And so, the conversations that take place in the meetings, on the practice field, you know, there's communication, verbal communication, but there's also is body like language communication within coaches. Like, "Hey, on that Got you." You know what I mean? There's a little bit like, "Yeah, I'm with you on that." cuz, you know, we've talked about it and we've built up reps together. Um, so, it's huge to have everyone back and, you know, looking forward to an exciting >> I heard you say elite communicator for Daniel Jones and then also for your coaching staff. I don't think that's an accident for for that group. >> Yeah. >> [laughter] >> Yeah, I think when you're together, you know, like like with anything, right? When you're with around somebody, you know, you get to know the person, um, the connection you build with that person, um, you got to be great at communication to be successful in this league. >> Having said that, how excited are you for the challenge of seeing this offense go against Sauce Gardner, Trevarius Ward, Cam Bynum, that the secondary during training camp? Cuz that I mean, that that seems to be a really good measuring stick for this group. >> Well, I'm excited about our defense on the back end. All the guys you just mentioned, those guys are really good football players. And so, it's going to be some really good back and forth with our offense and defense, uh, going through training camp. And it's going to be very competitive. And that's going to make us better as a football team as a whole, not just one side of the ball. It's going to make everybody better. So, we're looking forward to that. >> How do you watch the defensive line during training camp? Like, what do you look for from that group? >> Well, going back to communication again. I mean, with offensive line, you know, you got to be on the same page. And I think with the defensive line, too, you know, you got to be on the same page, too. You got to be gap sound. And when there's games going on, you got to be great at communicating right there. And then when you look at it individually, you know, you have one-on-one matchups, you know, can you win your one-on-one, uh, you know, consistently, you know? And then also how, you know, a three technique inside, you know, how's he taking on a double team? How's a nose guard taking on a double team? Can he anchor? I think that all goes into play, you know, when I'm watching those guys in practice and watching the film. >> What's something just about training camp that, and I don't want to ask you to, you know, be like, oh, what do fans not know about it? But like, what's something that you are really dialed in on in looking when you go back and you look at the practice tape? I feel like there's so many opportunities, so many playmakers, bro, like whoever get their opp, just know that they going to shine, and I feel like that's the that's the beauty of it, that's what you want, that's type of you want, that's type of player teammates you want, you know, anybody who can go on that field and go get you whatever you need, you know what I'm saying, and um man, just can't wait. Whole receiving room, man, bunch of dogs in We all going to push each other, going to get better every single day during this camp, man, and um and get get ready to go into the season, bro, you know, just can't wait, for sure. >> Me, ball always been life. 5 years old, I played with my dad, he was my coach. And then everything just after that. >> You were >> I was like 6 ft tall. I was that big. I was the youngest out there. >> Yeah. >> See how it feels and it ended up being just the best I ever And so I'm blessed for that. And um And then I played basketball as well, too. >> So it's natural like this. >> Played basketball as well. Um I love basketball career. I would have I would have loved to to play in the NBA. Um So I had two offers in basketball, TCU and NC State. So I was going to move to but my football career and football way better. But you know, football I started to talk to them. 10th grade football. Um First one was Southern Miss. Then NC State and then Tennessee. So I took a couple of things. So blessed for that. So I was of course starting coming out. And then I'm here. >> Let's go. Let's go. >> Great spring and uh everyone's so excited for you and uh what you'll do at camp. >> Competition with the time. >> Um yeah, I'm ready. I'm I'm >> Second prize >> can't wait. >> What What Yeah. >> [music] [music] >> Jalen, what's this off-season been like for you? They talk a lot about the growth from year one to year two. >> Yeah, a lot of growth for me. Whether that's just on the field, off the field, all those different things, but just building confidence with everything I do. Perfecting my my route running and just yeah, being ready to go for next season. Game changer, being able to make big plays. I think that's what I bring to the Texans. So, just go out there, roll, be myself and yeah. >> You had a lot of impact as a returner. How much do you like that they're still going to have you do the returns and have that kind of dual role for you? >> Oh, I love it. Anytime I can get the ball in my hands is another opportunity to change the game. So, them giving me that opportunity, I'm blessed and I'm excited to move forward with that. >> Nice shirt you're coming into. >> CJ, you could do a lot of things together. What do you expect from CJ this season? People talking about he's going to have a great year. >> Oh, different guy. Definitely different dude. Man on a mission. And he ready to fight. Corner doubling center of the way. >> You guys been out there working and getting ready. What's the excitement level like with the Texans? Everybody's excited about the draft, free agency. CJ looks good. He looks nice and lean. >> man. The excitement is great, man. I feel like we had a great draft. OTAs starting back up. Getting back in that mode, so I feel like the energy is great and I'm going to continue to go on our mission. Headed to the Super Bowl. So, it starts right now. >> Are you impressed with CJ? A lot of people, including DeMeco, have talked about it. He says he's locked in. It looks like he's hitting the weights. >> Yeah. I get off season time away. Everybody need off season get time away. But, he he look good. Everybody look great, man. I'm glad everybody's back. Tank Dell look good. I'm glad he's back now getting his groove back. And just all around, offense and defense, man. I'm glad everybody's back in the building and getting things down pat. >> You've been playing football for a long time. You've been a Texan for a long time. How much is something you'd like to be here the rest of your career if possible? And how how much would that be something that would just make you really happy? >> It would mean a lot, man. We know where we want to go. But, at the end of the day, we got to take one play at a time. You know, we got to move the sticks. We got to continue to put points on the board for the defense. You're on this arc of improvement. What can you do even better? And what are some things you're really proud of with your game that you feel like you've gotten down? >> I'm in a good place and I feel comfortable. Continue to find the things I need to improve on. title: Sean McVay, Byron Young & Matthew Stafford Recap The First Two Days Of Training Camp
text: Makua on a one-handed catch, but on two plays later, you got Trent McDuffy going strike for strike with him and just kind of the ying and yang of that. >> That's exactly right, Vinnie. And even the one that he made was an unbelievable throwing catch and guys are right in position. Um there was a lot of really high quality football and not necessarily worried about, you know, who's winning or losing the drill. Want to see good highc caliber ball. Want to see us be able to reset snap [music] after snap and I think that two-play sequence you're talking about is reflective of that. Uh there was a lot of really good plays, but what I think, you know, and even Matthew just said it when he broke the team down, we got a lot of guys that love football. You know, it's a blessing to be able to get out here um to be able to work hard, to work smart, to be able to protect one another, but push each other in a manner that's reflective of being able to have some productive failure on both sides of the football and um and that's what we want and I think that's what good teams do. >> Yesterday, yesterday Nate was talking about the pre- snap operation for Tai. What did you think about it yesterday? >> I thought yesterday was good. you know, I thought both he and Stat Sincer did a really nice job. There was a couple procedural issues, but I don't think it was a reflection of some of the things that those guys can control, but um you know, that's always going to be a big point of emphasis for us on both sides of the football and really in the kicking game and those snaps where we start with the football. And so, um I thought it was good and uh you know, that's always something that you can never pay close enough attention to. >> Sean, what are the expectations on you guys this year? How do you coach block out the noise? I think you acknowledge it, but you also talk about that that doesn't do anything. Let's be inside out. Um I think what's great is that people care about this game and and you guys have jobs to do and we respect that. But I reflect I respectfully say that your guys opinions doesn't mean to us, [laughter] you know. Um you know, but in all seriousness though, Omar, what I what I think is important though is that we're inside out. There's going to be adversity that inevitably we hit. How we handle that will be key. how we stay connected and how we continue to be courageous to to put ourselves out there with the unpredictability of what sports entails and that's part of being courageous and that's what we want and we've got a lot of guys that are wired the right way but I think you build skills in those areas and um and I feel really fortunate to do it with a group of people that have that mindset and mentality but we've got to earn it every single day >> you talk about that you appreciate being around these people you said it a lot last year that you love the guys that you were coaching when it's year 10 for you. How does that approach change? Do you feel even more appreciative of what you're doing? >> I think so. And I think part of it, Aaron, is is just based on the cycle of what's going on in your life. You know, I've mentioned it. Um, you know, having those two little boys and my wife, Veronica, you know, I do feel like it it makes you better and it gives you a better perspective. And a lot of the things, you know, the patience, the unconditional love, the things that you want to be reflective of as a parent are the same things that make you, you know, a good coach that you're supporting, you're trying to uplift people, you're challenging them because you love them and care enough about them to to do those types of things. But it's always has been and always will be about people. And I think what else is is very clear is as we've gotten the fortunate opportunity to go into year 10, you have an idea of the kinds of people that fit here and the kinds of people that motivate you and inspire you to not want to let them down and and we've got as many of those as we've ever had. Um we've had a really unique group of people over these years, but this has a chance to be as special of a collaboration of of people in terms of the players and the coaches that I've ever been around. >> How uping is it to play in front of these people today, in front of these kids? in front of the crowds that are here today, especially the children that are so loyal to the Rams. >> It's it's awesome. And and what what makes me really happy, too, is is seeing the heart that our players have to take time afterwards to be able to, you know, pay attention, sign an autograph, and and that's what it's about. And I think our guys, we have the right kind of guys that understand the the blessing of the platform they have to to be a positive influence. And I'm grateful for that. And John, when you look at those 10 years in this group that's been able to come together, how rare and special is that to have the cohesiveness and continuity to have the foundation that you're able to, you know, springboard off of? At this point, >> it is. And, you know, we've got a lot of guys that have played a lot of meaningful football. We've got some guys that, you know, Matthew, going into year 18, you know, we got five guys that are going into year 10 or later, and then we've got a lot of guys that are going into their fifth year that have accumulated or their fourth year that have accumulated a lot of snaps. And so, it's a special group. Um, you know, the thing that's so unique is just the volume of people you have is so much higher. And so, how we organically come together, how we allow people to be their their individual personalities, but still subscribing to the values that we uphold is going to be important. And we're in the middle of building that. And that's one of the most important things of training camp is how we come together as a team. And so far, I like the trajectory we're on. >> You you as a coach and and your staff, you're going to find the blemishes on the film of these last couple of days, but it's been a pretty high level first couple of days for you guys. It's only two days of course, >> but what does that say about where these the retention that these guys, you know, have from the spring to now and and their competitiveness? >> It's important to them. You know, Wade Phillips used to have a great saying, Vinnie, where if it's important enough to you, you'll get it done. And we've got guys that football's important to them, doing right by their teammates, having the communication, the operation, the urgency, and then being able to allow your gifts to come to life when the ball's snapped and and the cycle of the snaps unfolding. But, um, you're right, we can find a lot of things that we can correct. You know, there when you have 22 moving parts on every single snap and, uh, and these guys are trying to affect, you know, them in a negative way on the other side of the football, but it's been there's been some good quality football. Um, I've seen that and then I've seen some great learning opportunities for us as well. >> What a couple of the opportunities that the depth of your roster brings and what you want to get out of them like one or two priorities. Hey, this is at at the top of the list to get accomplished during the camp. >> Well, I think, you know, I think really it's coming together as a team. You know, I think it's understanding the importance of how we practice. We'll have two joint practices, one against the Saints, one against the Cowboys that our guys were counting on. That'll be basically their preseason. We'll get an opportunity to see a lot of the younger guys play in the preseason and those are great opportunities to play real football. When we put the pads on, it's close, but you're still not playing tackle football. Um, you know, and there's there's a couple spots. There's there's always important things that you want to be able to see unfold and and be able to establish some depth if, god forbid, you know, we have the inevitable injuries that do occur, but um we'll take it a day at a time and there's so many things. I could have you here all day if I talked about >> in a room full of stars, the wide receiver room, CJ Daniels is really turning heads. I know it's only the second day of practice, but what are you seeing out of him? >> He's done a good job. He's a mature rookie. I think u you know, I mentioned it in the spring when we talked about it. He's mature for a rookie. You can see he's come in nononsense mentality, but he enjoys football. And then he's really he's he's a great listener whether it's paying attention to his coaches with Rob, with yards, with Robert Woods, um with Nate Shield House, you know, and then he's got some incredible guys to learn from. Devonte Adams has such wisdom. Um and you know, and Fuka's had a lot of great experiences. Jordan Whittington is now becoming a veteran. So, it's a great group, but I'm excited about CJ and he'll be another guy, you know, when you talk about the importance of the preseason, he'll be a guy I'm looking forward to watching play and obviously in these practice settings as well. >> Coach, there are obviously a lot of >> This one them sto last two. This one is St. >> There obviously a lot of expectations around Ty Simpson. You see him out there today with Matthew Stafford. Can you talk about the encouragement that you put into him when you see him training out there with Stafford today? >> Yeah, he's doing a great job. You know, I think the best thing is is I think some of the leadership from our peers with Matthew pouring into that room with Tai, with Stson, you know, with Matthew, that's a that's a big deal. And uh and Dave Regone does a great job leading that room. Um having played the position, having the capacity and the understanding of what it looks like to do it at a high level consistently day after day. And so I think Tai's in a great situation to be around some great people to learn from. >> Sean, the uh the approach you took with Stson and Tai today um with this being Matthew's first practice of camp. Y >> is that something that's going to be reflective every time Matthew practices in terms of how you allocate those reps or how do you look at >> Yeah, I I would say this. You know, I don't want to pigeon hole myself into one size approach. You know, Stson got, you know, the majority of those reps with the second group today, but Ty came in and did a nice job with the one set that he did have. Um, you know, and we'll we'll just kind of continue to evaluate, but, you know, being able to figure out what that looks like is important. I think both those guys have done a nice job and and obviously having number nine out there, he looked pretty damn sharp, so it was good to have him. >> Thanks, coach. >> Thank you, guys. want to get a shot. >> Oh, there. >> All right. What was this offseason like for you? What did you kind of focus on? What you what you get to do in the time off? >> Uh, it's been good. You know, uh, just been, you know, nurse out my knee. Uh, that was a process. Um, you know, they got good plan for you in place. But, you know, offseason been good. Spent some time with family, but overall, you know, feeling real good. >> What is the plan with your knee? >> Uh, you know, just day by day, you know, uh, practice yesterday. um don't want to do too much and overload on workload. So, you know, uh we got a plan just, you know, take some time and, you know, get back out there um in a couple of days. But, you know, just day by day, you know, we trying to last for 17 games and postseason. So, >> how much of a challenge was that? Was it? Yeah. Was it the same knee as you injured in the playoffs and what how much of a challenge was that to deal with at that time of year? >> Uh yes, it's the same knee. Um you know, it was challenging, but at the same time, you know, I trust the training staff and you know, everything. And you know, I've been something I was dealing with for, you know, years now. And, you know, uh, they always came through for me and, you know, I trust them. So, >> is there a sense of unfinished business around here, uh, from last season and even greater expectations because as deep as your roster is? >> Uh, 100%. You know, every year we, you know, we we, uh, we don't accomplish and we'll be better every year. Um, expectations. Um, you know, definitely got a chip on our shoulder. you know, uh, over the years how hard we work and every year you see we've been getting better and we came up short last year and this year, you know, our goal is to take it all the way and finish the job. So, >> have you talked to Sean said Aaron Donald's thinking about, you know, whether or not he wants to do this and come back. Have you talked to him at all and you thought about what it would look like while you guys out there and the opportunities you'd have to get to? Uh, >> I haven't talked to him, you know, I haven't talked to him, you know, just thinking about that, reminiscing about my rookie year and um, you know, playing with him and, you know, it was amazing experience and just getting that opportunity to play one the first year, it was a blessing. So, you know, of course I wouldn't, you know, I would definitely love playing with him again, you know, with Miles right there and the D line we already had. So, you know, that that would be a dream come true, but at the same time, you got understand, you know, uh, one of the greatest ever doing and, you know, he he put his time in. So, you know, whatever he decide, you know, I'm always on his side. I'm just thankful for that. >> How would you describe if he does come back what you guys would look like as a group? >> Um, you know, you know, that just got to wait and see, I'll say, you know, got to wait and see. don't want to just, you know, put expectations out there, but definitely, you know, uh just it will be a joy to watch for sure. >> What's something you learned from from Aaron your rookie year that that you still use to this day? >> Uh just being patient, understanding that uh uh every play writes his own story. You know, uh every play going to be different. You know, if you make a mistake, just put that play behind you and just make up for it. But just be patient, you know, just understand mistakes going to happen and just just learn from it. >> What's it been like to get to know Miles Garrett? What do you, if any, what have you picked up from him so far? uh you know just his mindset you know him talking in the meeting room and just watching him play in practice you know it's it's amazing his art you know uh just what love watching him play after one practice you know just if you seen him out there and his mindset on getting off the ball and winning reps and you know just you know his point of view of everything it's different so uh just picking his brain and just trying to learn from the best you know it's definitely thankful for having this opportunity though for sure >> the other side of that you know trade was losing a guy like Jared verse so what was that like for you in the process you know having come up with him and and see him go to another team. >> Uh yeah, that was uh that was unfortunate. You know, uh it's part of business. Uh it's something that definitely did hit me pretty hard. Uh you know, building that relationship with him. Uh you know, friendship, you know, that was a brother to me, you know, still a brother, you know, at the same time. I just had to understand that that's kind of how it goes. Uh you know, like I said, unfortunately, we didn't want that to happen. At the same time, you know, I got to keep going. I got to do my job. Um it wasn't my fault. You know, it happened. I wouldn't want that to happen. Um, and you know, the upside, we did get a great players also. So, you know, can't can't be upset about that either, but just uh definitely wish it could have gone another way, but at the same time, that's part of business and that's kind of how it goes. Uh, just also thankful to have Miles on my team. >> how's the room different Jared? >> Uh, I'll say it's a lot quieter. [laughter] >> Yeah, Jared, he he bring that energy. He always talking. Uh, you know, he he talks non-stop. even if he's wrong, he's still going to [laughter] he's still going to gaslight you and make you feel like you was wrong. Uh but you know, you definitely will be missed, you know, at the same time. Uh having Miles in the room, uh Miles, you know, he he changing the culture also, you know, uh y'all, we were about to leave yesterday and um we were just about to leave. He said, "We not going to break it down." And I was just like, "Oh, we bring it down in me." So, yeah, we're going to bring it down in here. So, I said, "Okay." You know, that's that's a piece of the culture that he's bringing on. So, you know, definitely fun to talk to him and stuff like that. is being on the field yet where you're like, "Wow, that's that's why you're >> every rep." So, you know, uh, just watching every day. what is your relationship with Josiah Stewart and kind of what is you know how have you seen him grow so far in his young career? Uh, you know, it's great, you know, uh, from his rookie year to now and just seeing the type of player he is and he want to be better and just develop new moves and, you know, I be picking his brain, too. So, >> Byron, with the relationships that you have been able to cultivate when the business of football rears his ugly head, how do you process and and compartmentalize the the personal relationships versus the business of the game? >> Uh, you know, that it' be tough. Uh, you just can't take everything personal. I said that you got to take a couple of days for yourself. I had to understand was Bennis, you know, talking to the coaches and understand like at the end of the day, it weren't personal. They was just doing what best for they feel like was best for the team and that's all I can respect them for. You know, at the end of day, they have a job. They can't use their feelings or personality into it. They just got to, you know, do what they do all for the best of the team. At the end of the day, you know, I got to respect them and trust them. So, >> every guy, >> last one. What are your thoughts about being in a contract year and what this what this year could mean for you, your contact with the Rams, any of that? >> Uh, the way I see it, regardless, I'm going have to play out this year. Um, you know, everything going to uh work itself out. You know, it's part of the game, but you know, regardless if I don't get a contract right now, later on, I still got to play this year. Um you know, wasn't out here yesterday, was able to kind of uh you know, watch and and see these guys do their thing, but it was fun to be back out here today. Um trusting the process kind of that we've come up with. Um you know, Coach McVey, Reggie, and all his staff uh doing everything they can to try to help our team be as good as we possibly can, but also help me um you know, peak at the right time, be ready to rock and roll come week one. But uh it was a blast to be out here today. Um, you know, I'm surrounded by so many great players and I don't take that for granted both on our side of the football and on the defensive side. It is, uh, you know, it's a blessing to come out here every single day and compete against these guys and and play with the guys on on the offensive side of the ball. But um I'm just doing everything I can to make sure that uh my body and my mind feel as good as I possibly can. Um every time I'm out here, obviously you guys know I'm giving it everything I got and and trying to raise uh you know raise the level of play and and and help our guys be as good as we possibly can as a team. Um but uh I don't I don't think it's probably worth getting too much into days one and three and and all that kind of stuff. Matt, at this stage of your partnership with the Rams and Shan Bay, how much of it is kind of retention carryover and how much of it is, oh wow, he really did put 100 new players in. >> No, there's some new stuff and there's some old stuff that's called something different or what a old word was makes means something new. So, he's always keeping me on my toes. You know, you give that guy too much time in the offseason, there's going to be some tweaks and some fun stuff to come back to. But, you know, that's what we love. He's always thinking about trying to put us in the best position to succeed. And if you're a player, man, what more could you want from a coach? and not only the X's and O's, but you know, he spends a lot of time thinking about us as people and us as a team and how yeah, do we want to go win a bunch of football games and be really successful? Absolutely. But we also want to cultivate an environment where we can all become better people and better men and uh he obviously sets a great example for that um for all of us. Matthew, when you've been when you've been in the league as long as you have, what is the training set training camp mindset for you now compared to a few years ago? Is it any different? >> Yeah, I think it definitely um you know, it definitely morphs um as you get a little bit uh older. I want to continue to try to play at a high level, but I want to elevate the guys around me too, right? I want to help our defense. I want to help our offense and and try to push our team. And the fun thing for me is, I mean, I look around and there's so many guys doing the same thing, right? Like I'm doing my best. If everybody does our best, um, we're going to continue to make each other better. And that's that's the goal. >> What's it like? Go ahead. Mike, >> do you you mentioned all the allp pro guys you guys added on defense. You now have the MVP and reigning defensive player of the year in the same team for the first time in history. Do you believe in iron sharp as iron that these reps and the reps you'll have in practice will make both sides of the ball better when it comes to >> Yeah, absolutely. It's, you know, can't help but make each other better. Um, as long as everybody comes out with the right attitude and the right expectation to go out there and go to work, um, you know, pieces of paper and names on a roster, you know, those don't win football games. Teams and players and groups do. And so, um, we're doing everything we possibly can to continue to, you know, Sean said it the other night, you know, we we've got a potentially a high ceiling, right? We've got great players, like you said, that have done a lot in this league. Um, what can we do to continue to raise our floor, right? So, if hey, I'm off a little bit, you know, we can still go find a way to win a football game. Or if our defense is off a little bit, we can still find a way to go win a football game. And continuing to raise that floor is something that, um, you know, I think is going to be a huge part of our journey in this season. And listen, it's it's day one for me out here. The interesting thing is, and this is why I can't wait to get to training camp to see how he's going to call this defense because when you look at what he had in Detroit, Derek Barnes was so big for what Aaron Glenn wanted to do because he was so versatile. Calvin Pace was so versatile in Rex Ryan's defense because he could play this Sam backer, but he could also be on the edge in a traditional 34. That's what Derek Barnes did. So, like when they were multiple, you hear Aaron Glenn talk about, you know, variation when it comes to the defensive front, front variation. That's what he means being multiple, being able to put out multiple fronts up front. But he was able to do that in Detroit because he had a guy like Derek Barnes. The Jets were able to do that when I was playing because we had a guy like Calvin Pace. I mean, if he doesn't if if it's a bad year for him, I I they the guaranteed money I think is either up or almost all of it is up after this year and it would not be like really it wouldn't kill the Eagles in 2027 if he was >> I feel I feel like an 11th bonus question Mosher would be is Jake Elliott safe but they didn't bring anybody in to compete with him. >> No, this is definitely something we talked about on that'll be on tomorrow's podcast. I mean, they gave him a pay cut, okay? He agreed to a pay cut. So, that's your first sign that there's a lack of confidence cuz guess what? They don't cut your pay if they really really really happy with you. His numbers tell I mean he was down to what? 76, 74% accuracy from 94, 95% 3 years ago which was a steep drop and it's been 2-year drop. So, I think that they don't want to rattle him mentally by bringing in somebody right now, you know, after having him take a pay cut but 2-3 weeks in the camp if they're bringing a kicker in and the job watch is on. >> Like he's going to be on the he's still making a lot of money but they might force them to say we need to carry a veteran kicker on the practice squad just in case and if that's the case then you know that the end is near. Well, the Birds report tomorrow and we've got you covered on Football at Four, the Inside the Birds podcast. They've got you covered all season long. Another season of Football at Four. It all kicks off tomorrow, the Birds report Wednesday. They are scheduled most likely to be on the field weather permitting according to Mosher the weatherman but they will be out there sometime this week. Mosher will not be. He is heading on a little vacation before the Birds get on to the field. So, Mosher have a great vacation and rest of the week and we will talk to you when you get back, man. >> Appreciate you. Have a great one.

title: Evaluating the Patriots Secondary & Squad Depth After Day 3 of 2026 Training Camp
text: The Patriots had a walk-through on day three, but don't worry, we're here to break down what we've seen over the first three days of Patriots training camp. Let's get into it. >> [music] >> Welcome to the Patriots Training Camp Cast presented by New Balance. Day three, Ev, they went down to a walk-through, not a ton to see. >> Didn't sound too too excited about that, Mike. >> I was excited about it, though. It seemed like they were getting a little bit into third down, you know, we were seeing both sides of the ball putting some tweaks in, still some first, second down stuff. So, you know, thought this was an opportunity maybe to regroup a little bit in just how we're feeling about things. First, though, generally, heard from Mike Vrabel this morning. You were in there, I was out pumping the crowd up. What did you take away from Vrabel this morning? >> Yeah, a lot of Gaybackus questions, as you could imagine, about his contract and reports about his contract, but I think the biggest takeaway was, you know, somebody asked him if he was in jeopardy of missing the season or anything like that, and he said that he doesn't anticipate that at all. So, I I think that we're hoping that we're going to see Gaybackus sooner rather than later. It seems like that's the general sentiment. Some off-season award winners, if you're into that sort of thing. >> it. >> A lot of the year two guys got recognized. Will Campbell, Jared Wilson, Kyle Williams, and Elijah Ponder were the four guys that they gave off-season awards to. So, Vrabel just highlighting the fact that last year's rookies really came in this off-season and stepped things up. >> Yeah, important players, too. I mean, guys you're looking forward to hopefully make a jump, especially Elijah Ponder here as we see, you know, Akers, Landry, hopefully they work their way back in. Little housekeeping, though. Reggie Gilliam back at the walk-through. Of course, it's just a walk-through, but I think he said it was a veteran rest day, is that right? >> a maintenance day. I think some of these guys, Morgan Moses, was another one that he put in this category, but I wouldn't be surprised if we see a lot of those older guys, Hunter Henry, Morgan Moses, you know, players like that, that some days they might not do as much as others. >> You got to get your fullback ready for that day one of pads when you're going to put probably put the ball on the goal line and there's going to be some some collisions going on. Uh but you know, overall Ev, we've now watched three practices and you know, admittedly pads are going to come on this week. So, we're all excited for that, but still a lot to take away and I I would just start with the secondary. Think you have most of those guys coming back. You added Kevin Byard coming off his third All-Pro season, led the NFL seven interceptions. We've seen those guys active early. Thankfully, Kristian Gonzalez has been out there participating, but he's been around the ball. We you know, heard from A.J. Brown today talking a little bit about their match-up on the first day. Craig Woodson comes up with an interception. We heard from him today. You know, felt good to get his hands on the ball this early in camp. Carlton Davis with a pass break-up yesterday. And Romeo Doubs right down the line. And you know, even Rasul Douglas just flying all over the place. I mean, his speed and how they use him just really impressive. Early days of camp, to me these guys are the key takeaway. They've been kind of dominating. >> Yeah, it feels like all off-season cuz we as we do, we talk about the concerns and things that might prevent us from, you know, hoisting a Lombardi trophy in February. And uh we talked so much about pass rush and the lack of edge rushers and things like that. Well, it helps when you're you know, the quarterback has to hold the ball because the secondary is, you know, got everybody locked down. So, I think that that's what you're hoping is that there's a lot invested in this back end uh with Kristian Gonzalez maybe even being more invested in Kristian Gonzalez here soon, but Carlton Davis is under contract. Marcus Jones is under contract. You signed Byard. You draft Woodson. So, there's a lot of guys that they've invested a lot in and I think you what you hope is that the playoffs last year were a precursor to what's going to happen this season where you can blitz a little bit more. You can get exotic up front to get guys free in the pass rush even though you don't necessarily have that Myles Garrett type. Maybe the quarterback having to hold the football a little bit extra, uh that will allow the pass rushers to get home. >> Second thing I want to talk about is just the wide receiver group cuz I think it's a really stacked group and you know, we talked a lot about Keishawn Boutte this off-season. And here's Keishawn Boutte first two two days of practice coming down with tough catches. It's what he does. Just keep showing up, keeps making plays, but you know, I just see I watch have you got the two fields going. They've got Kyle Williams going. They've got Mack Hollins. They've got Pop Douglas heavily involved. Of course, all eyes are on A.J. Brown and and Romeo Doubs, the new guys, to see how they're fitting in, but you know, this is a year where not just the talent has improved, but they still have a lot of depth, and I'm just that's what I'm most curious about going through camp. How does that all play out, and who ends up sticking and really being the core guys that they're going to roll with? >> Yeah, it's a good point, and I I feel like at times in practice, I see guys running with groups that I wouldn't expect them to run with cuz there's so much depth there that they just need to get Mack Hollins a rep. So, he might be repping with Tommy DeVito. And you're like, wait a second, Mack Hollins is a veteran guy in this league that caught the only touchdown in the Super Bowl the Patriots scored, and he's repping with the twos and threes. That's a little odd, but they have so much depth at that position as you mentioned, and I'll admit it, all offseason I've been kind of on the trade Keashawn Boutte train, but he's winning me over, and I think you two things. One, he he deserves a lot of credit for that. He deserves a lot of credit for showing up, and I think he showed up the same way in mini camp, in shape, and just making plays, and making it impossible to move on from him. And I think he deserves a lot of credit for that. And the other thing, you know, you see him, A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs moving around the formation a lot, and guys running routes out of the slot, sometimes running routes outside, and I'm starting to see, okay, maybe we can figure this thing out where, you know, Keashawn Boutte, sometimes he's the big slot, sometimes A.J. Brown's the power slot, and they just kind of move off that X position a little bit more than what they have in their past. So, I'm warming up to it. I think that there's a, you know, they're exploring different ways to try to get all three of those guys on the field at the same time. >> Last thing, Drake May. I mean, let's talk about him a little bit. Yesterday, Kevin Byard said, "Defense usually starts out a little bit in front of the offense." I mean, I I thought over those two practices, I mean, he made some throws, but I think he also missed some throws. I think he, you know, there was a there was a blitz yesterday, Carlton Davis off the edge. It looked like they kind of got him on that one. Um maybe a little bit of a a slow start for Drake. I mean, I don't want to push the panic button or anything like that. We just heard from A.J. Brown who's like, "Yeah, they're not really letting him throw it yet." So, you know the best is still yet to come. Uh but I think he's kind of set the stage here for this second week of training camp as we get the pads on. We start to look forward to joint practices for, you know, Drake, A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs start to turn up the volume a little bit and start making some some plays. >> Yeah, I thought what A.J. Brown said about him not really throwing the ball a ton yet I kind of rung true to me because it's just he's a rhythm quarterback. And I think that, you know, it might be hard for him uh going to get three reps here, three reps there, and then we're going to hand it off, and like all these different things that they're doing and they don't just play. And at some point in training camp, we're going to get a string of 18 straight Drake Maye reps and we'll we'll see the real Drake Maye that we saw all of last season. So, I'm not concerned about it by any means. I would also mention A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, a little bit of Eli Raridon, too. New faces, new guys that he's throwing the football to. Uh so, I think that if I'm not concerned, but if there's one thing I want to see a little bit more of, it's some chemistry with those new guys. I think that all three of those guys, especially Brown and Doubs, it might be a little bit of a slower burn in before we start to see them really efficient and and hitting on all cylinders cuz they're getting used to each other. And that's another thing that Brown talked about was communication and knowing where the ball's going to be if the coverage is in a certain area and you know, those little details that right now that's the time of year to work it out. >> Yeah. >> All right. Well, that's day three of walkthrough. Probably ramp the pace up a little bit more on Tuesday. We think uh Wednesday will be an off day, and then we're looking at pads at the end of this week as we continue to ramp up in training camp. So, we'll be back tomorrow with more takeaways from Patriots training camp.

title: A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Morgan Moses & More Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: AJ, we saw you having fun with the crowd. One hand catch, what have you. How how comfortable are you here? What's it been like so far with this process? >> Um, I'm still getting comfortable each and every day. And I'm grateful. The offense is uh I'm pretty I'm pretty in a good spot, you know. I want to say I'm like 90 90%. You know, um and it's just really just about going to executing and getting on the same page with Drake each and every day. But I'm I'm really comfortable. >> How would you define your growth since you last played for the Raiders of Tennessee? >> Oh man, I've matured a lot, man. And uh as I as you get older, you learn from your mistakes and you grow from those things and and um you know, football is football at the end of the day, you know. But as far as like as the man aspect, you know, you learn from your mistakes and you grow from them. >> How would you define your relationship with Drake right now? What goes into creating that optimal wide receiver quarterback relationship? >> Nonstop communication, you know, just hearing what he thinks and you know, and he's listening to me and we're just trying to get on the same page. >> Guys since training camp like you've been going up against Gonzo quite a bit, what have you seen from him so far? >> Oh, stud. You know, everybody knows Gonzo's a stud. You know, each and every day, you know, whenever I got to go against him, you know, the the margin of error is very small, you know, and that's what you want. And those are my matchups, so I don't shy away from those and you know, CD as well, you know. So it's good on good and we're making each other better, you know. I mean, we're in competition right now, but it's all for the greater good for the team. >> What do you like about this offense? >> Uh the variety. The variety, I can't get into all that. Y'all know that. [laughter] Yeah. I'm still working on answering prayers, man. Yes, it is a blessing, man. I come to work at each and every day with a smile on my face. You know, I'm around great guys, great energy, you know, pushing pushing each other to be great, you know, and holding each other accountable. So. >> Now having to got to spend some time with Dre, what about his game? What about his approach to practice and things like that that impresses you most? >> Uh true professional. True professional in the way he goes about his business. Um they're not really letting him throw the ball right now, which is you know, but uh we'll get going as as camp progresses, you know, so. >> There's been a couple of moments when you guys haven't been able to connect on targets. >> Yeah. >> What are the small tweaks you guys have to make to make sure that those are completions? >> Um again, just being on the same page, communication maybe uh angle here that may I may need to go uh the higher or something something small like that cuz it's it's a the details are very small in this league and you know, you got to execute and so, you know, as yesterday something something so small and it may be the angle and you know, tips and overthrows, you know, it goes other way, you know, that's how the game go. >> How's your relationship with Mike Vrabel? You know, when he had you in Tennessee, you were 21, 22, 23 now. >> 29? >> I'm 29, I'm 29. >> Mhm. >> How's it evolved over time? >> Um just knowing that uh it comes from a genuine place, you know, uh like the first first team meeting, you know, he had ripped me for almost bringing in a catch, you know, and uh he expects me to make that play and uh you know, early on as a as a rookie, you know, I was didn't really like that too much, you know, but uh now I know it comes from a great place and he expects me to make that play and so do I as well. >> Does playing with a new quarterback change the way you play the position? >> Oh, you have to. You have to. You You have to do what your quarterback likes, you know. >> how are you starting to change the way you play so far? >> Uh I mean, as far as as my game, my game will be my game. Um but as far as of what he what he likes and what he needs, that's that's the things that I got to get on the same page with him and continue to work on those things and we will and we have so. >> This morning coach Vrabel said um was asked about your knee and you said that maybe some things were fabricated. >> Yeah. People make things up. Just how frustrating was that this offseason and just how good are you feeling now? >> Um it's not frustrating at all because I don't pay no mind to it, you know, I don't give life to it, so. >> When you look at the group you have, AJ, Dobbs, and Cobb, >> Oh, what excites you about this wide receiver >> No, just guys just working hard, you know, uh you know, may not have the biggest name, but you guys just full of grit, full of grit and coming to work each and every day, and you know, and uh we all hold each other accountable, and it's fun. It's a great group. >> Is there anything unique >> I can't get into that. You've been with Vrabel longer than me. >> [laughter] >> When it comes to red zone efficiency, it's been a big point of emphasis for this team. How can you and how do you look for opportunities to make this team a more efficient and better team in the red zone? >> In the red zone, uh you know, timing and space, and it's going to be it's going to be tight coverage, you know, uh throws on time, you got to catch make catches in traffic, you know, um simple. >> What's the time in North Carolina at training camp in the hotel? >> Yeah. Yeah, it was uh it was real helpful, you know, uh we spent 3 days down there. Um, and we got after it, you know, um it was pouring rain, but we it was it was we were still at it. Yeah. >> AJ, just wanted to clarify something you said. Mike pointed out a catch that you thought you should have had. Was that from the Was that from the first day of >> That's the first That's the first day of practice. Yeah. >> And that was Christian that was >> Uh-huh, yeah. Uh just just bring it in, you know, I did the hard part. I I caught it away from my body, and just bring it in with my other hand, you know, uh you know, Vrabel doesn't care about style points, and I don't either, you know, uh so maybe he thought that I was just trying to get the crowd going or something, but it's Vrabel, you know, so you just, you know, take everything with a grain of salt, and you know, listen to him, and and shoot, just make the catch, you know, so. >> Speaking of Vrabel, about him? We're seeing him I know it's just a walk-through, but we're seeing him today in the pads. Like he's getting after it with you guys. What's it like to have a coach who does stuff >> Yeah, he thinks he still can play. Yeah, he took like Allen 30 in the workout yesterday. >> Yeah, he thinks he still can play, but it's cool. It's cool. He walks around with the animosity and he challenges guys and no, it's cool to see. It's fun. >> Is he talking about 90% of that or about the playbook physically? >> Playbook. Playbook. Absolutely. >> Can you explain the footwear? >> The footwear? >> Oh, these are my little muffin shoes, toe shoes. They're very comfortable. You know, I try to work out and I'm not even supposed to tell you all that. >> Yeah, why do your production typically comes outside of the most you've seen you, but Rule mentioned that at some point he's going to use the inside as >> Does anything change about your vision and your pre-snap process when you're on the outside versus when you're on the inside? >> You know, absolutely. You know, uh on the outside I'm I'm I'm really scanning the safeties and then I'm looking to the corner then I'm back at the safeties and and obviously, you know, on the inside I'm looking at the backers and I'm going to the safeties and seeing the seeing if it's the coverage is rotating and and what I have to do because my route may change in the slot. So. >> What stood out to you the most about your time with Drake in North Carolina? It was off field stuff more important than on field stuff in some ways? Like how did that What stood out to you the most in those memories? >> What stood out? That those guys go stay up all night. Yeah, I was in the bed 9:30. Yeah, >> and they were loud. But, you know, Drake is Drake, man. He does a great job. He comes to work. He's prepared and he's a true professional. You know, he can make any throw. So, we're excited and we just continue to try to keep getting better. >> Signed a long time >> Two questions in your final thoughts? >> What's that relationship like for you >> with the fans? >> Um I'm I'm here to make plays and you know, try to build this relationship, you know, uh let let it happen organically. >> Is it exciting? >> question. >> DeAndre Hopkins, what's it like to have >> Hop, yeah. Um it was cool. It was cool to have him the first few days and um you know, just trying to pick his brain as much as possible. I think he played like 13 years, so whenever I'm around someone or anyone that can give me any type of knowledge about the game or off the field, you know, I'm going to listen. So, um uh yeah. Thank y'all. >> You know, first interception of training camp yesterday, just kind of walk me through the emotions and how it felt to just really be back out there. >> Yeah, I mean it's a blessing to be out here. Uh you know, this is something that you know, you got to take uh you know, advantage of the opportunity. Can't take for granted. Um and just getting that first interception it felt good. Hopefully we can get some more rolling in as the practice is going. >> Greg, is there anything you've taken from Kevin Byard so far in the little time you've been teammates cuz he's played a long time in the system obviously. >> Yeah, I mean it's more so just in the film room like just hearing him break down things, just you know, what he's seeing uh scheme-wise and different coverages and how he's able to like play stuff. Just hearing all of that is just interesting to hear and uh I'm just trying to take it in as he, you know, keep on spitting game to me, so. >> Was there one thing that he might have pointed out that surprised you or you hadn't considered before? >> Not yet. Nothing that is like actually surprised me. It's kind of, you know, back some of the basic stuff. Some things is like kind of just key things that, you know, I don't want to spill out, so yeah. >> same lines, he's he's been very consistent keeping everybody playing, you know, in every game. What have you learned on that side as well? >> Yeah, I mean I'm just watching his routine is pretty good. Uh you know, he does the contrast, does the sauna, does massages, everything else and that's stuff that I've been doing as well, so um you know, we're pretty similar when it comes to that. >> Anything uh surprise you or impress you with this this receiving core between A.J. and Romeo and and the guys that are coming back? >> Uh no, I knew that they would make plays. Um you know, those are all guys who can, you know, go up and get the ball, uh whatever the cost may be. They put it on film already, so that's nothing that I didn't expect. >> With Gonzales and A.J. Brown, I mean, that's like people would tune into that match up every week. You know, but here it is on the field every day. >> Is that fun for you to get ready for that? >> fun. It's definitely fun just to, you know, look at the match up, look at it on film, you know, see who's winning the reps or not. But, you know, those are two great guys who is at the top of their position, so that's just cool to have on your team. >> Is it sometimes the defense is a little ahead of the offense at this time of the the off-season? Are you guys at the point where you're starting to outsmart the offense with with scheme stuff yet or or is that you waiting for that till later in camp? >> No, I mean, I don't think there's any like outsmarting. I think, you know, both sides come to play every day. We come to compete and, you know, sometimes they may win, sometimes we may win. That's just how the game goes, but the the good thing about it is we all competing, we're all trying to get better, just all trying to build chemistry, so that's the best thing about it. >> Greg, what did your performance in the Super Bowl do, if anything, for you heading into the off-season? >> Yeah, definitely gave me confidence knowing that I can, you know, play with the best of the best and play at a high level, so just going into, you know, this season, I'm just, you know, riding on that confidence knowing that I can go make plays and, you know, I don't got to be out there playing timid or anything. >> What's the biggest difference between the guy we saw playing in that game and and you here now? >> Biggest difference? I mean, I have a lot of rest on my hands. You know, I had a whole off-season to rest and recover and, you know, this is just a new season. I'm ready to go. >> Greg, you didn't last year it's like kind of a whole different you know, wondering how that extra college experience helped prepare you for the NFL. I mean, kind of like you said, I kind of have experience under my hands, but honestly, I don't think it really like, you know, did anything more than anybody else. Um I know I I handled business, put in the the time in the playbook and everything else, and I mean, it just worked out last year. >> Treylon said yesterday that he feels more relaxed in this training camp. >> He's not a rookie, he doesn't feel like he needs to be perfect about everything. How do you How do you feel about sort of your comfort level going into your second year? >> Yeah, I mean, I feel the same way. I mean, at this point you kind of know the playbook, you know how things are going to go. Um you know that there's competition every every snap, every down, and um now it's just going out there and making plays and having fun with it cuz, you know, last year you had a kind of like a chip on your shoulder being a rookie and trying to make the team and do stuff like that, but uh now it's just relax and just out there playing, building chemistry with the whole defense, so it just feels fun. >> Speaking of year two, uh coach Gore, second year, you know, an official title now with the coordinator. What have you just seen from him since last season ended to what it's been like working this year? >> Yeah, I mean, I think Zach knows that, you know, what we did last year, we had a lot of good things on film, and uh he's just trying to build on that, just trying to enhance it, and I think going into this year, uh he feels pretty good about, you know, where we are, and uh I think we all just want to keep on building. Uh wasn't a significance at all. Um I honestly wanted a single-digit number. Uh I wanted to get out of 31, so once Kevin came, it was the perfect time for me to get out of that, so uh yeah, it's no real significance. >> How did that negotiation go? >> It went good, you know, he gave me a call, kind of talked about it a little bit, and, you know, we're here now. That's all I can say. >> We'll do one more. >> Guys, I just see Mack talk about how sometimes when veterans come in with a lot of experience, some people ask a lot of questions, some people want to give their distance. What's your relationship been like with Kevin Byard this preseason so far? >> Yeah, I mean, ever since he's been here, I've been asking him questions, just kind of trying to pick his brain a little bit on, you know, how he plays stuff, and uh also it's just kind of watching him and just building that chemistry, just, you know, when we're out there, just trying things, and uh once we get to the film room, we'll talk about it like, "Hey, what'd you see here? Like, what was your thought process on this?" And just kind of having those conversations just, you know, help you develop and and build on your game. >> That's great. >> Appreciate y'all, man. God bless. >> Mario, how has the summer been for you and and how do you feel like it's going? >> No, summer's been good, you know, uh new motto, we've been putting in that pain and I feel like uh this summer's been good. >> Putting in the pain? >> Putting in that pain. Uh we're just working out and one of my boys like, "Ooh, this that pain." I'm like, "Yeah, this that pain." So, you know, uh so I've always been saying, you know, we got to put in that pain so later we have that joy. So, uh we're going to put in that pain now so you know, later end of this year, you know, that's when that joy come. >> It's been a lot of competition at receiver this summer. How does that help you guys? >> Oh, that makes the room better, you know, um all the, you know, the depth that we have and man, the competition, man, it just makes, you know, the next person better. Like I've been saying like, you know, the past the since last year, you know, our room been stacked and uh feel like that's been making, you know, the next person better. >> What have you seen from A.J. Brown? >> Man, uh great leadership, you know, uh don't say much but if you watch what he do, it's it's it it's very like glorifying, you know, just just watching him do what he does and it it it helps. It helps, you know, just like lead by example, you know, but don't get me wrong, he does say stuff in the in the room that us younger guys definitely need to know, you know, to widen up widen up our, you know, our I'd say our brain but just to see what he what he says and does, it's amazing. >> What about route running? Like, what are some of the things you can learn? >> Yeah, just uh say route running but also like a defense, you know, he'll be like, "Man, if you see this, man, it trust me, it'll be this." And it does and it's just a different perspective. >> I'm just curious with your role this year. This is the first time you're going to have the same offensive coordinator 2 years in a row. Do you feel like there's more of an opportunity they'll carve out like a specific role in this offense cuz he's moved around a lot like maybe slot or having some more opportunities there? >> Uh I really want to say like uh it just built confidence, you know, uh going into the offense a second year. Man, you go in there with I say more swagger, you know, uh last year, you know, just learning the play and then go out there, you know, sometimes you're going to go out there with a little hesitation. Now, you know, knowing the playbook and getting deeper into it, knowing more than what you knew, it's just a man, I feel like that helps a lot and go out there with that confidence. Man, you play with that swagger that a lot of people haven't seen because you've been in different offenses. >> Talk when you talked about that touchdown he mentioned specifically how much you've grown when it comes to decision routes and consistency there. What's your perspective there and how have you kind of evolved in that area of your >> Yeah, like like I said, just being in my second year of this offense, you know, all my years I've had a different offense and had to learn a different offense. So, uh being in this offense for a second year, man, I finally get to dive deeper into the into the offense. >> Second year in the offense and third year with Drake. Where do you feel like your chemistry's at with Sam? Is that something you feel like you guys maybe hit another level with this year? >> Man, uh chemistry is there, you know, uh just you know, uh speaking with Drake, man, his terminology different, you know, and uh man, he he's into this offense a lot, man. Confidence is up there and uh I feel like I've been seeing it grow and grow. This year has definitely been like uh you know, just like, you do it. And he he's been doing it, man. It's just seeing him in practice, man, it it it lifts me up, you know, just just to see the growth and uh it's amazing to see what he's doing. >> You talk about the competition in the wide receiver room. title: Mike Macdonald On The Team's Early Training Camp Progress | Seattle Seahawks
text: All right. I love this cadence, you know, every other day. Pretty good. Another great day. You know, it's these days when the 12s are all out here, it's uh really special, but uh today was still great. Weather's awesome. Guys are in good spirits. Uh a lot of stuff we need to work on. We're not uh got a long way to go, but um you know, just let's focus on what we got to do next, you know. So, I'd like to finish practice a little bit better uh tomorrow to finish out this ramp period and then uh we'll get a day off and be back in pads on Thursday. So, what do you got? Well, there's I mean, there's always things you're finding that you want to that you want to do a better job of. I think we have a pretty clear vision about how we want to operate, you know, given the circumstance and uh you know, you hit it, that's great. What's the you know, let's go hit it again the next day. If you don't, then you know, we fall short. What can we do better to to go to go hit it the next day? So, I think it's just there's these there's all these little you know, benchmarks that you're that you're trying to hit and uh and you know, we're doing a good job. We're doing a good job. It's we're trying to refining ourselves. We got a lot of young guys getting a lot of good reps. So, a lot of good stuff going on. The tempos are a little funky right now. It's um not a lot of like challenge at the catch point, you know, it's not as not as physical as it will get, which is which is good, you know. The guys are getting their legs underneath them and they're sore right now. So, um and we're dealing with a few things, but uh kind of par for the course on that front. >> People talk about blitzes versus not sending people, um but you guys also just send different people. How do you think about blitzing versus uh rush variety? >> Like I'm talking about on like uh dropback situations? Well, I think you need to have the threat of bringing people, you know, if you if you're if you're not uh if you're not able to bring second and third level players, then I think that uh probably makes the offense's job a little too easy. But um it's kind of like what's what are we really good at? What what you know, how do we want to attack this offense? Sometimes it's a little bit more a little bit more pressure, sometimes it's a little bit more four-man rush. Uh but it's not like we're going into a game saying, "Hey, we have to operate at a certain like cadence or pattern or something like that." I think that kind of limits you a little bit too much. >> How would you evaluate Bell as a blitzer? Do you >> Good. Yeah, he's done a good job. I mean um he didn't have any opportunities during last year's last season, but I remember in the preseason he did a good job when he got those ops and um he's an athletic guy. He's he's powerful, you know, he's not as big as Nick, but he's he's pretty pretty dang strong, too. And he can and he can run and um he's really good near the line of scrimmage. I I I just remember being bummed that uh that he wasn't going to be here. So, you're trying not to make too much of the situation, just kind of make the best decision at that point now that that he got claimed. It fortunately happens more than you want when we when we lose some of our own guys. >> Dontae Powell was talking with us earlier. >> How good is he in the discipline of the game? >> Yeah. >> You know, kind of shout out the strength and conditioning. So, just now he's getting on the field, what have you seen out of Dontae so far? >> Yeah, you can definitely feel him today. Uh it's you want to affect the quarterback, but not too much at this point. It's part of the training camp, so uh uh he's doing great. He's doing great. He's uh getting used to how we roll here and I think I think he's enjoying his time, which is a positive, but uh definitely definitely seen flashes for sure. So, we're excited about it. >> This is the first time you get to see Riley Mills out here for training camp practices. He had a couple of splashy plays today there late in the set. Uh how have you seen him progress here now that he's actually getting to be on the field and not be sitting on the >> happy for him. I know he's excited. I mean, he he's the type of guy that you're going to feel his spirit out here and his competitiveness. And again, there's there's things part of his game that we're going to always be attacking and he's he's going to take advantage of his opportunities. I mean, he's putting in the extra work. Um he's kind of like a football junkie, you know? And I feel that the whole process is what honestly is probably the most what you respect about him the most is the amount of work that he's willing to put in, you know, kind of behind the scenes to come out here and and and perform and execute. So, uh he's off to a good start. >> You said uh Julian Neil that we saw him come off the field. >> Yeah, we had a couple guys today um that we we just took in that didn't seem like anything major, but we're going to get them checked out and see what we need to do. >> You mentioned how you like having Jack here and has it changed perspective at all or helped perspective to have a someone around that probably cares more about the trucks out there than the Super Bowl? >> Well, not I mean, that was the that was that was uh the way Jack was about 5 minutes after the Super Bowl. So, nothing's really changed on that front. He's a little more like aware of what's going on this training camp than he was last training camp, so that's pretty cool to for him to kind of see stuff around here and get excited about it, but you know how it is when you're a parent, just see your kid light up about anything, you're like, "Okay, this is the coolest thing ever." And so, when when it's um you know, when we're when we're playing our our real games, it's just we're just doing what we've been practicing this whole time. >> My show's going to be up in a second. He had a career year last year. >> Who's that again, though? >> Ernest Jones. >> Okay. >> What can you say about what he did for you last year? What he did for you last year? All the interceptions. >> Yeah. Yeah. I don't know. I couldn't say I mean, I we love E.J. All three coaches. It's kind of like kind of like our new players on on our team. I know we've gone against him plenty of times and he's not an easy guy to get out of the C gap. He can he can block and he's got a pretty good route tree and route after the catch. He's a big dude. So um just get talking to him briefly. So far he seems like he's excited to be here. He's locked in in meetings and stuff, which I always appreciate to see that he's doing a good job. >> What have you seen from Jadarian over the first three days? >> Yeah, he's um he's a big like is it is is it tough to evaluate right now? Kind of, you know, without with the tempos and things and see how like the runs finish. But you can see the decisiveness, you can see the the movement ability, like the quickness, the speed. Um doing a lot of great things in pass protection, which I you know, I appreciate. So um I you know, it's positive right now. Just really excited about him. He's got a great opportunity in front of him. I know I know Ham's coaching his tail off and and so I think we're in a we're just in a good spot right now, you know, but it'll be interesting to see how it how it shakes out when we start getting some some more, you know, more realistic type looking reps. >> How much film did you have on his pass protection at Notre Dame? They said he didn't do much of it and what did you >> It's tough. It's tough. We'll see, but right now there's not a lot of things that you're, you know, checking off of stuff that he can't do that you think that he can't do. He's He's been really I mean, he's been tremendous.
